[lineWidth](#plotOptions.boxplot.lineWidth) option.

In styled mode, the stem stroke width can be set with the
`.highcharts-boxplot-stem` class.

name: plotOptions-boxplot-threshold
title: threshold
description:
The Y axis value to serve as the base for the columns, for
distinguishing between values above and below a threshold. If `null`,
the columns extend from the padding Y axis minimum.

name: plotOptions-boxplot-whiskerColor
title: whiskerColor
description:
The color of the whiskers, the horizontal lines marking low and high
values. When `undefined`, the general series color is used.

In styled mode, the whisker stroke can be set with the
`.highcharts-boxplot-whisker` class.

name: plotOptions-boxplot-whiskerDashStyle
title: whiskerDashStyle
description: The dash style of the whiskers.

name: plotOptions-boxplot-whiskerLength
title: whiskerLength
description:
The length of the whiskers, the horizontal lines marking low and
high values. It can be a numerical pixel value, or a percentage
value of the box width. Set `0` to disable whiskers.

name: plotOptions-boxplot-whiskerWidth
title: whiskerWidth
description:
The line width of the whiskers, the horizontal lines marking low and
high values. When `undefined`, the general
[lineWidth](#plotOptions.boxplot.lineWidth) applies.

In styled mode, the whisker stroke width can be set with the
`.highcharts-boxplot-whisker` class.

name: plotOptions-bubble
title: bubble

name: plotOptions-bubble-animationLimit
title: animationLimit
description:
If there are more points in the series than the `animationLimit`, the
animation won't run. Animation affects overall performance and
doesn't work well with heavy data series.

name: plotOptions-bubble-colorByPoint
title: colorByPoint
description:
When using automatic point colors pulled from the global
[colors](colors) or series-specific
[plotOptions.bubble.colors](series.colors) collections, this option
determines whether the chart should receive one color per series or
one color per point.

In styled mode, the `colors` or `series.colors` arrays are not
supported, and instead this option gives the points individual color
class names on the form `highcharts-color-{n}`.

name: plotOptions-bubble-displayNegative
title: displayNegative
description:
Whether to display negative sized bubbles. The threshold is given
by the [zThreshold](#plotOptions.bubble.zThreshold) option, and negative
bubbles can be visualized by setting
[negativeColor](#plotOptions.bubble.negativeColor).

name: plotOptions-bubble-marker-fillOpacity
title: fillOpacity
description: The fill opacity of the bubble markers.

name: plotOptions-bubble-marker-symbol
title: symbol
description:
A predefined shape or symbol for the marker. Possible values are
"circle", "square", "diamond", "triangle" and "triangle-down".

Additionally, the URL to a graphic can be given on the form
`url(graphic.png)`. Note that for the image to be applied to
exported charts, its URL needs to be accessible by the export
server.

Custom callbacks for symbol path generation can also be added to
`Highcharts.SVGRenderer.prototype.symbols`. The callback is then
used by its method name, as shown in the demo.

name: plotOptions-bubble-maxSize
title: maxSize
description:
Maximum bubble size. Bubbles will automatically size between the
`minSize` and `maxSize` to reflect the `z` value of each bubble.
Can be either pixels (when no unit is given), or a percentage of
the smallest one of the plot width and height.

name: plotOptions-bubble-minSize
title: minSize
description:
Minimum bubble size. Bubbles will automatically size between the
`minSize` and `maxSize` to reflect the `z` value of each bubble.
Can be either pixels (when no unit is given), or a percentage of
the smallest one of the plot width and height.

name: plotOptions-bubble-negativeColor
title: negativeColor
description:
When a point's Z value is below the
[zThreshold](#plotOptions.bubble.zThreshold)
setting, this color is used.

name: plotOptions-bubble-sizeBy
title: sizeBy
description:
Whether the bubble's value should be represented by the area or the
width of the bubble. The default, `area`, corresponds best to the
human perception of the size of each bubble.

name: plotOptions-bubble-sizeByAbsoluteValue
title: sizeByAbsoluteValue
description:
When this is true, the absolute value of z determines the size of
the bubble. This means that with the default `zThreshold` of 0, a
bubble of value -1 will have the same size as a bubble of value 1,
while a bubble of value 0 will have a smaller size according to
`minSize`.

name: plotOptions-bubble-softThreshold
title: softThreshold
description:
When this is true, the series will not cause the Y axis to cross
the zero plane (or [threshold](#plotOptions.series.threshold) option)
unless the data actually crosses the plane.

For example, if `softThreshold` is `false`, a series of 0, 1, 2,
3 will make the Y axis show negative values according to the
`minPadding` option. If `softThreshold` is `true`, the Y axis starts
at 0.

name: plotOptions-bubble-zMax
title: zMax
description:
The minimum for the Z value range. Defaults to the highest Z value
in the data.

name: plotOptions-bubble-zMin
title: zMin
description:
The minimum for the Z value range. Defaults to the lowest Z value
in the data.

name: plotOptions-bubble-zThreshold
title: zThreshold
description:
When [displayNegative](#plotOptions.bubble.displayNegative) is `false`,
bubbles with lower Z values are skipped. When `displayNegative`
is `true` and a [negativeColor](#plotOptions.bubble.negativeColor)
is given, points with lower Z is colored.

name: plotOptions-bullet
title: bullet

name: plotOptions-bullet-dragDrop-draggableTarget
title: draggableTarget
description: Allow target value to be dragged individually.

name: plotOptions-bullet-targetOptions
title: targetOptions
description: All options related with look and positioning of targets.

name: plotOptions-bullet-targetOptions-borderColor
title: borderColor
description:
The border color of the rectangle representing the target. When
not set, the point's border color is used.

In styled mode, use class `highcharts-bullet-target` instead.

name: plotOptions-bullet-targetOptions-borderRadius
title: borderRadius
description: The border radius of the rectangle representing the target.

name: plotOptions-bullet-targetOptions-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description:
The border width of the rectangle representing the target.

In styled mode, use class `highcharts-bullet-target` instead.

name: plotOptions-bullet-targetOptions-color
title: color
description:
The color of the rectangle representing the target. When not set,
point's color (if set in point's options -
[`color`](#series.bullet.data.color)) or zone of the target value
(if [`zones`](#plotOptions.bullet.zones) or
[`negativeColor`](#plotOptions.bullet.negativeColor) are set)
or the same color as the point has is used.

In styled mode, use class `highcharts-bullet-target` instead.

name: plotOptions-bullet-targetOptions-height
title: height
description: The height of the rectangle representing the target.

name: plotOptions-bullet-targetOptions-width
title: width
description:
The width of the rectangle representing the target. Could be set
as a pixel value or as a percentage of a column width.

name: plotOptions-column
title: column

name: plotOptions-column-borderColor
title: borderColor
description:
The color of the border surrounding each column or bar.

In styled mode, the border stroke can be set with the
`.highcharts-point` rule.

name: plotOptions-column-borderRadius
title: borderRadius
description:
The corner radius of the border surrounding each column or bar. A number
signifies pixels. A percentage string, like for example `50%`, signifies
a relative size. For columns this is relative to the column width, for
pies it is relative to the radius and the inner radius.

name: plotOptions-column-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description:
The width of the border surrounding each column or bar. Defaults to
`1` when there is room for a border, but to `0` when the columns are
so dense that a border would cover the next column.

In styled mode, the stroke width can be set with the
`.highcharts-point` rule.

name: plotOptions-column-centerInCategory
title: centerInCategory
description:
When `true`, the columns will center in the category, ignoring null
or missing points. When `false`, space will be reserved for null or
missing points.

name: plotOptions-column-colorByPoint
title: colorByPoint
description:
When using automatic point colors pulled from the global
[colors](colors) or series-specific
[plotOptions.column.colors](series.colors) collections, this option
determines whether the chart should receive one color per series or
one color per point.

In styled mode, the `colors` or `series.colors` arrays are not
supported, and instead this option gives the points individual color
class names on the form `highcharts-color-{n}`.

name: plotOptions-column-colors
title: colors
description:
A series specific or series type specific color set to apply instead
of the global [colors](#colors) when [colorByPoint](#plotOptions.column.colorByPoint) is true.

name: plotOptions-column-cropThreshold
title: cropThreshold
description:
When the series contains less points than the crop threshold, all
points are drawn, even if the points fall outside the visible plot
area at the current zoom. The advantage of drawing all points
(including markers and columns), is that animation is performed on
updates. On the other hand, when the series contains more points than
the crop threshold, the series data is cropped to only contain points
that fall within the plot area. The advantage of cropping away
invisible points is to increase performance on large series.

name: plotOptions-column-dataGrouping-groupPixelWidth
title: groupPixelWidth
description:
The approximate pixel width of each group. If for example a series
with 30 points is displayed over a 600 pixel wide plot area, no grouping
is performed. If however the series contains so many points that
the spacing is less than the groupPixelWidth, Highcharts will try
to group it into appropriate groups so that each is more or less
two pixels wide. Defaults to `10`.

name: plotOptions-column-dataLabels-y
title: y
description:
The y position offset of the label relative to the point in
pixels.

name: plotOptions-column-depth
title: depth
description: Depth of the columns in a 3D column chart.

name: plotOptions-column-dragDrop-dragHandle
title: dragHandle
description: Options for the drag handles available in column series.

name: plotOptions-column-dragDrop-dragHandle-cursor
title: cursor
description:
The mouse cursor to use for the drag handles. By default this is
intelligently switching between `ew-resize` and `ns-resize` depending on
the direction the point is being dragged.

name: plotOptions-column-dragDrop-dragHandle-pathFormatter
title: pathFormatter
description:
Function to define the SVG path to use for the drag handles. Takes
the point as argument. Should return an SVG path in array format. The
SVG path is automatically positioned on the point.

name: plotOptions-column-edgeColor
title: edgeColor
description:
3D columns only. The color of the edges. Similar to `borderColor`, except it
defaults to the same color as the column.

name: plotOptions-column-edgeWidth
title: edgeWidth
description: 3D columns only. The width of the colored edges.

name: plotOptions-column-groupPadding
title: groupPadding
description: Padding between each value groups, in x axis units.

name: plotOptions-column-groupZPadding
title: groupZPadding
description: The spacing between columns on the Z Axis in a 3D chart.

name: plotOptions-column-grouping
title: grouping
description:
Whether to group non-stacked columns or to let them render
independent of each other. Non-grouped columns will be laid out
individually and overlap each other.

name: plotOptions-column-maxPointWidth
title: maxPointWidth
description:
The maximum allowed pixel width for a column, translated to the
height of a bar in a bar chart. This prevents the columns from
becoming too wide when there is a small number of points in the
chart.

name: plotOptions-column-minPointLength
title: minPointLength
description:
The minimal height for a column or width for a bar. By default,
0 values are not shown. To visualize a 0 (or close to zero) point,
set the minimal point length to a pixel value like 3\. In stacked
column charts, the length is applied to each point in isolation, so
tightly packed values may overlap. See the stacked sample below for a
plugin that lays out the stack as a whole instead.

name: plotOptions-column-pointPadding
title: pointPadding
description: Padding between each column or bar, in x axis units.

name: plotOptions-column-pointRange
title: pointRange
description:
The X axis range that each point is valid for. This determines the
width of the column. On a categorized axis, the range will be 1
by default (one category unit). On linear and datetime axes, the
range will be computed as the distance between the two closest data
points.

The default `null` means it is computed automatically, but this
option can be used to override the automatic value.

This option is set by default to 1 if data sorting is enabled.

name: plotOptions-column-pointWidth
title: pointWidth
description:
A pixel value specifying a fixed width for each column or bar point.
When set to `undefined`, the width is calculated from the
`pointPadding` and `groupPadding`. The width effects the dimension
that is not based on the point value. For column series it is the
horizontal length and for bar series it is the vertical length.

name: plotOptions-column-states-hover
title: hover
description:
Options for the hovered point. These settings override the normal
state options when a point is moused over or touched.

name: plotOptions-column-states-hover-borderColor
title: borderColor
description:
A specific border color for the hovered point. Defaults to
inherit the normal state border color.

name: plotOptions-column-states-hover-brightness
title: brightness
description:
How much to brighten the point on interaction.

In styled mode, the hover brightening is by default replaced
with a fill-opacity set in the `.highcharts-point:hover`
rule.

name: plotOptions-column-states-hover-color
title: color
description: A specific color for the hovered point.

name: plotOptions-column-states-select
title: select
description:
Options for the selected point. These settings override the
normal state options when a point is selected.

name: plotOptions-column-states-select-borderColor
title: borderColor
description: A specific border color for the selected point.

name: plotOptions-column-states-select-color
title: color
description: A specific color for the selected point.

name: plotOptions-column-threshold
title: threshold
description:
The Y axis value to serve as the base for the columns, for
distinguishing between values above and below a threshold. If `null`,
the columns extend from the padding Y axis minimum.

name: plotOptions-columnpyramid
title: columnpyramid

name: plotOptions-columnrange
title: columnrange

name: plotOptions-columnrange-dataLabels
title: dataLabels
description:
Extended data labels for range series types. Range series data labels
have no `x` and `y` options. Instead, they have `xLow`, `xHigh`,
`yLow` and `yHigh` options to allow the higher and lower data label
sets individually.

name: plotOptions-columnrange-dragDrop-draggableHigh
title: draggableHigh
description: Allow high value to be dragged individually.

name: plotOptions-columnrange-dragDrop-draggableLow
title: draggableLow
description: Allow low value to be dragged individually.

name: plotOptions-contour
title: contour

name: plotOptions-contour-colorKey
title: colorKey
description:
This must be set to `'value'` to make the colorAxis track with the contour
plot.

name: plotOptions-contour-contourInterval
title: contourInterval
description:
The interval between contour lines. Determines the spacing of value
levels where lines are drawn on the plot. By default, the interval is
calculated using the value range.

name: plotOptions-contour-contourOffset
title: contourOffset
description:
The offset for contour line positioning. Shifts the contour levels so
lines and bands are drawn at `contourOffset + n * contourInterval`
instead of `n * contourInterval`.

Example: with `contourInterval: 10` and `contourOffset: 5`, levels are
at 5, 15, 25, etc. Use this to align levels with a reference value
without changing the data. Non-positive values are treated as 0.

name: plotOptions-contour-lineColor
title: lineColor
description: The color of the contour lines.

name: plotOptions-contour-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description:
This setting controls the visibility and size of contour lines. For now,
only '1' and '0' are valid options, effectively controlling the
visibility of the lines.

name: plotOptions-contour-marker-states-hover-lineColor
title: lineColor
description: Color of the marker outline. Defaults to `'black'`.

name: plotOptions-contour-marker-symbol
title: symbol
description:
A predefined shape or symbol for the marker. When undefined, the
symbol is pulled from options.symbols. Other possible values are
`'circle'`, `'square'`,`'diamond'`, `'triangle'`,
`'triangle-down'`, `'rect'`, `'ellipse'`, and `'cross'`.

Additionally, the URL to a graphic can be given on this form:
`'url(graphic.png)'`. Note that for the image to be applied to
exported charts, its URL needs to be accessible by the export
server.

Custom callbacks for symbol path generation can also be added to
`Highcharts.SVGRenderer.prototype.symbols`. The callback is then
used by its method name, as shown in the demo.

name: plotOptions-contour-smoothColoring
title: smoothColoring
description:
Whether to use gradually transitioning color gradients between contour
levels. When disabled, each contour level is filled with a single flat
color.

name: plotOptions-cylinder
title: cylinder

name: plotOptions-dependencywheel
title: dependencywheel

name: plotOptions-dependencywheel-borderRadius
title: borderRadius
description:
The corner radius of the border surrounding each node. A number
signifies pixels. A percentage string, like for example `50%`, signifies
a relative size. For nodes this is relative to the node width.

name: plotOptions-dependencywheel-center
title: center
description:
The center of the wheel relative to the plot area. Can be
percentages or pixel values. The default behavior is to
center the wheel inside the plot area.

name: plotOptions-dependencywheel-dataLabels-distance
title: distance
description: Distance between the data label and the center of the node.

name: plotOptions-dependencywheel-dataLabels-format
title: format
description:
A format string for data labels of the links between nodes. Available
variables are the same as for `formatter`.

name: plotOptions-dependencywheel-dataLabels-formatter
title: formatter
description:
Callback to format data labels of the links between nodes. The `format`
option takes precedence over the `formatter` option.

name: plotOptions-dependencywheel-dataLabels-nodeFormat
title: nodeFormat
description:
The format string specifying what to show for nodes in the sankey
diagram. By default the nodeFormatter returns `{point.name}`. Available
variables are the same as for `nodeFormatter`.

name: plotOptions-dependencywheel-dataLabels-nodeFormatter
title: nodeFormatter
description:
Callback to format data labels of nodes in the dependency wheel. The
`nodeFormat` option takes precedence over the `nodeFormatter` option.

name: plotOptions-dependencywheel-size
title: size
description: Size of the wheel in pixel or percent relative to the canvas space.

name: plotOptions-dependencywheel-startAngle
title: startAngle
description: The start angle of the dependency wheel, in degrees where 0 is up.

name: plotOptions-dumbbell
title: dumbbell

name: plotOptions-dumbbell-connectorColor
title: connectorColor
description:
Color of the line that connects the dumbbell point's values.
By default it is the series' color.

name: plotOptions-dumbbell-connectorWidth
title: connectorWidth
description:
Pixel width of the line that connects the dumbbell point's
values.

name: plotOptions-dumbbell-lowColor
title: lowColor
description:
Color of the start markers in a dumbbell graph. This option takes
priority over the series color. To avoid this, set `lowColor` to
`undefined`.

name: plotOptions-dumbbell-lowMarker
title: lowMarker
description:
Options for the lower markers of the dumbbell-like series. When `lowMarker`
is not defined, options inherit form the marker.

name: plotOptions-dumbbell-states-hover-connectorWidthPlus
title: connectorWidthPlus
description: The additional connector line width for a hovered point.

name: plotOptions-errorbar
title: errorbar

name: plotOptions-errorbar-color
title: color
description:
The main color of the bars. This can be overridden by
[stemColor](#plotOptions.errorbar.stemColor) and
[whiskerColor](#plotOptions.errorbar.whiskerColor) individually.

name: plotOptions-errorbar-linkedTo
title: linkedTo
description:
The parent series of the error bar. The default value links it to
the previous series. Otherwise, use the id of the parent series.

name: plotOptions-errorbar-whiskerWidth
title: whiskerWidth
description:
The line width of the whiskers, the horizontal lines marking
low and high values. When `null`, the general
[lineWidth](#plotOptions.errorbar.lineWidth) applies.

name: plotOptions-funnel
title: funnel

name: plotOptions-funnel-animation
title: animation
description: Initial animation is by default disabled for the funnel chart.

name: plotOptions-funnel-borderRadius
title: borderRadius
description:
The corner radius of the border surrounding all points or series. A
number signifies pixels. A percentage string, like for example `50%`,
signifies a size relative to the series width.

name: plotOptions-funnel-center
title: center
description:
The center of the series. By default, it is centered in the middle
of the plot area, so it fills the plot area height.

name: plotOptions-funnel-dataLabels-inside
title: inside
description:
Whether to render the data label inside the funnel item instead of
outside, connected by a connector line.

name: plotOptions-funnel-height
title: height
description:
The height of the funnel or pyramid. If it is a number it defines
the pixel height, if it is a percentage string it is the percentage
of the plot area height.

name: plotOptions-funnel-neckHeight
title: neckHeight
description:
The height of the neck, the lower part of the funnel. A number
defines pixel width, a percentage string defines a percentage of the
plot area height.

name: plotOptions-funnel-neckWidth
title: neckWidth
description:
The width of the neck, the lower part of the funnel. A number defines
pixel width, a percentage string defines a percentage of the plot
area width.

name: plotOptions-funnel-reversed
title: reversed
description:
A reversed funnel has the widest area down. A reversed funnel with
no neck width and neck height is a pyramid.

name: plotOptions-funnel-states
title: states
description: Options for the series states.

name: plotOptions-funnel-states-select
title: select
description: Options for a selected funnel item.

name: plotOptions-funnel-states-select-borderColor
title: borderColor
description: A specific border color for the selected point.

name: plotOptions-funnel-states-select-color
title: color
description: A specific color for the selected point.

name: plotOptions-funnel-width
title: width
description:
The width of the funnel compared to the width of the plot area,
or the pixel width if it is a number.

name: plotOptions-funnel3d
title: funnel3d

name: plotOptions-funnel3d-gradientForSides
title: gradientForSides
description:
By default sides fill is set to a gradient through this option being
set to `true`. Set to `false` to get solid color for the sides.

name: plotOptions-funnel3d-height
title: height
description:
The height of the series. If it is a number it defines
the pixel height, if it is a percentage string it is the percentage
of the plot area height.

name: plotOptions-funnel3d-neckHeight
title: neckHeight
description:
The height of the neck, the lower part of the funnel. A number
defines pixel width, a percentage string defines a percentage
of the plot area height.

name: plotOptions-funnel3d-neckWidth
title: neckWidth
description:
The width of the neck, the lower part of the funnel. A number defines
pixel width, a percentage string defines a percentage of the plot
area width.

name: plotOptions-funnel3d-reversed
title: reversed
description:
A reversed funnel has the widest area down. A reversed funnel with
no neck width and neck height is a pyramid.

name: plotOptions-funnel3d-width
title: width
description:
The max width of the series compared to the width of the plot area,
or the pixel width if it is a number.

name: plotOptions-gauge
title: gauge

name: plotOptions-gauge-dataLabels
title: dataLabels
description:
Data labels for the gauge. For gauges, the data labels are
enabled by default and shown in the center.

name: plotOptions-gauge-dial
title: dial
description:
Options for the dial or arrow pointer of the gauge.

In styled mode, the dial is styled with the
`.highcharts-gauge-series .highcharts-dial` rule.

name: plotOptions-gauge-dial-backgroundColor
title: backgroundColor
description: The background or fill color of the gauge's dial.

name: plotOptions-gauge-dial-baseLength
title: baseLength
description:
The length of the dial's base part, relative to the total
radius or length of the dial. Accepts a pixel value if given
as a number, or a percentage value if given as a percentage
string. If the base length is greater than 0, the dial's base
will have an even width, before it narrows in to the top.

name: plotOptions-gauge-dial-baseWidth
title: baseWidth
description:
The width of the base of the gauge dial. The base is the part
closest to the pivot, defined by baseLength. Accepts a pixel
value if given as a number, or a percentage value if given as
a percentage string.

name: plotOptions-gauge-dial-borderColor
title: borderColor
description:
The border color or stroke of the gauge's dial. By default,
the borderWidth is 0, so this must be set in addition to a
custom border color.

name: plotOptions-gauge-dial-borderRadius
title: borderRadius
description: The border radius of the gauge dial

name: plotOptions-gauge-dial-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description: The width of the gauge dial border in pixels.

name: plotOptions-gauge-dial-path
title: path
description: An array with an SVG path for the custom dial.

name: plotOptions-gauge-dial-radius
title: radius
description:
The radius or length of the dial, relative to the radius of
the gauge itself. Accepts a pixel value if given as a number,
or a percentage value if given as a percentage string.

name: plotOptions-gauge-dial-rearLength
title: rearLength
description:
The length of the dial's rear end, the part that extends out
on the other side of the pivot. Accepts a pixel value if
given as a number, or a percentage value of the dial's length
if given as a percentage string.

name: plotOptions-gauge-dial-topWidth
title: topWidth
description:
The width of the top of the dial, closest to the perimeter.
The pivot narrows in from the base to the top. Accepts a
pixel value if given as a number, or a percentage of the dial
radius if given as a percentage string.

name: plotOptions-gauge-overshoot
title: overshoot
description:
Allow the dial to overshoot the end of the perimeter axis by
this many degrees. Say if the gauge axis goes from 0 to 60, a
value of 100, or 1000, will show 5 degrees beyond the end of the
axis when this option is set to 5.

name: plotOptions-gauge-pivot
title: pivot
description:
Options for the pivot or the center point of the gauge.

In styled mode, the pivot is styled with the
`.highcharts-gauge-series .highcharts-pivot` rule.

name: plotOptions-gauge-pivot-backgroundColor
title: backgroundColor
description: The background color or fill of the pivot.

name: plotOptions-gauge-pivot-borderColor
title: borderColor
description: The border or stroke color of the pivot.

name: plotOptions-gauge-pivot-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description: The border or stroke width of the pivot.

name: plotOptions-gauge-pivot-radius
title: radius
description:
The radius of the pivot, the center point of the gauge.
Accepts a pixel value if given as a number, or a percentage
of the full gauge radius if given as a percentage string.

name: plotOptions-gauge-showInLegend
title: showInLegend
description:
Whether to display this particular series or series type in the
legend. Defaults to false for gauge series.

name: plotOptions-gauge-wrap
title: wrap
description:
When this option is `true`, the dial will wrap around the axes.
For instance, in a full-range gauge going from 0 to 360, a value
of 400 will point to 40. When `wrap` is `false`, the dial stops
at 360.

Defaults to `undefined`, which is equivalent to `true` when
the axis ranges over 360 degrees, and `false` when less.

name: plotOptions-heatmap
title: heatmap

name: plotOptions-heatmap-animation
title: animation
description: Animation is disabled by default on the heatmap series.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-borderRadius
title: borderRadius
description:
The border radius for each heatmap item. The border's color and
width can be set in marker options.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description: The border width for each heatmap item.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-color
title: color
description:
The main color of the series. In heat maps this color is rarely used,
as we mostly use the color to denote the value of each point. Unless
options are set in the [colorAxis](#colorAxis), the default value
is pulled from the [options.colors](#colors) array.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-colsize
title: colsize
description:
The column size - how many X axis units each column in the heatmap
should span.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-interpolation
title: interpolation
description: Make the heatmap render its data points as an interpolated image.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-marker-states-hover-height
title: height
description: Set the marker's fixed height on hover state.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-marker-states-hover-heightPlus
title: heightPlus
description:
The number of pixels to increase the height of the
selected point.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-marker-states-hover-lineWidthPlus
title: lineWidthPlus
description: The additional line width for a hovered point.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-marker-states-hover-width
title: width
description: Set the marker's fixed width on hover state.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-marker-states-hover-widthPlus
title: widthPlus
description:
The number of pixels to increase the width of the
selected point.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-marker-states-select-height
title: height
description: Set the marker's fixed height on select state.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-marker-states-select-heightPlus
title: heightPlus
description:
The number of pixels to increase the height of the
selected point.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-marker-states-select-width
title: width
description: Set the marker's fixed width on select state.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-marker-states-select-widthPlus
title: widthPlus
description:
The number of pixels to increase the width of the
selected point.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-marker-symbol
title: symbol
description:
A predefined shape or symbol for the marker. When undefined, the
symbol is pulled from options.symbols. Other possible values are
`'circle'`, `'square'`,`'diamond'`, `'triangle'`,
`'triangle-down'`, `'rect'`, and `'ellipse'`.

Additionally, the URL to a graphic can be given on this form:
`'url(graphic.png)'`. Note that for the image to be applied to
exported charts, its URL needs to be accessible by the export
server.

Custom callbacks for symbol path generation can also be added to
`Highcharts.SVGRenderer.prototype.symbols`. The callback is then
used by its method name, as shown in the demo.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-nullColor
title: nullColor
description:
The color applied to null points. In styled mode, a general CSS class
is applied instead.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-pointPadding
title: pointPadding
description: Padding between the points in the heatmap.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-rowsize
title: rowsize
description: The row size - how many Y axis units each heatmap row should span.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-states-hover-brightness
title: brightness
description:
How much to brighten the point on interaction.

In styled mode, the hover brightening is by default replaced
with a fill-opacity set in the `.highcharts-point:hover`
rule.

name: plotOptions-histogram
title: histogram

name: plotOptions-histogram-binWidth
title: binWidth
description:
Width of each bin. By default the bin's width is calculated as
`(max - min) / number of bins`. This option takes precedence over
[binsNumber](#plotOptions.histogram.binsNumber).

name: plotOptions-histogram-binsNumber
title: binsNumber
description:
A preferable number of bins. It is a suggestion, so a histogram may
have a different number of bins. By default it is set to the square
root of the base series' data length. Available options are:
`square-root`, `sturges`, `rice`. You can also define a function
which takes a `baseSeries` as a parameter and should return a
positive integer.

name: plotOptions-item
title: item

name: plotOptions-item-endAngle
title: endAngle
description:
In circular view, the end angle of the item layout, in degrees where
0 is up.

name: plotOptions-item-innerSize
title: innerSize
description:
In circular view, the size of the inner diameter of the circle. Can
be a percentage or pixel value. Percentages are relative to the outer
perimeter. Pixel values are given as integers.

If the `rows` option is set, it overrides the `innerSize` setting.

name: plotOptions-item-itemPadding
title: itemPadding
description:
The padding between the items, given in relative size where the size
of the item is 1.

name: plotOptions-item-layout
title: layout
description:
The layout of the items in rectangular view. Can be either
`horizontal` or `vertical`.

name: plotOptions-item-rows
title: rows
description:
The number of rows to display in the rectangular or circular view. If
the `innerSize` is set, it will be overridden by the `rows` setting.

name: plotOptions-item-startAngle
title: startAngle
description:
In circular view, the start angle of the item layout, in degrees
where 0 is up.

name: plotOptions-line
title: line

name: plotOptions-line-legendSymbol
title: legendSymbol
description:
What type of legend symbol to render for this series. Can be one
of `areaMarker`, `lineMarker` or `rectangle`.

name: plotOptions-lollipop
title: lollipop

name: plotOptions-lollipop-grouping
title: grouping
description:
Whether to group non-stacked lollipop points or to let them
render independent of each other. Non-grouped lollipop points
will be laid out individually and overlap each other.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph
title: networkgraph

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-dataLabels-format
title: format
description:
The
[format string](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting)
specifying what to show for _node_ in the networkgraph. In v7.0
defaults to `{key}`, since v7.1 defaults to `undefined` and
`formatter` is used instead.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-dataLabels-formatter
title: formatter
description:
Callback JavaScript function to format the data label for a node.
Note that if a `format` is defined, the format takes precedence
and the formatter is ignored.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-dataLabels-linkFormat
title: linkFormat
description:
The
[format string](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting)
specifying what to show for _links_ in the networkgraph.
(Default: `undefined`)

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-dataLabels-linkFormatter
title: linkFormatter
description:
Callback to format data labels for _links_ in the sankey diagram.
The `linkFormat` option takes precedence over the
`linkFormatter`.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-dataLabels-linkTextPath
title: linkTextPath
description:
Options for a _link_ label text which should follow link
connection. Border and background are disabled for a label that
follows a path.

**Note:** Only SVG-based renderer supports this option. Setting
`useHTML` to true will disable this option.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-draggable
title: draggable
description: Flag to determine if nodes are draggable or not.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-layoutAlgorithm-approximation
title: approximation
description:
Approximation used to calculate repulsive forces affecting nodes.
By default, when calculating net force, nodes are compared
against each other, which gives O(N^2) complexity. Using
Barnes-Hut approximation, we decrease this to O(N log N), but the
resulting graph will have different layout. Barnes-Hut
approximation divides space into rectangles via quad tree, where
forces exerted on nodes are calculated directly for nearby cells,
and for all others, cells are treated as a separate node with
center of mass.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-layoutAlgorithm-attractiveForce
title: attractiveForce
description:
Attraction force applied on a node which is connected to another
node by a link. Passed are two arguments:
- `d` - which is current distance between two nodes
- `k` - which is desired distance between two nodes

In `verlet` integration, defaults to:
`function (d, k) { return (k - d) / d; }`

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-layoutAlgorithm-enableSimulation
title: enableSimulation
description:
Experimental. Enables live simulation of the algorithm
implementation. All nodes are animated as the forces applies on
them.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-layoutAlgorithm-friction
title: friction
description:
Friction applied on forces to prevent nodes rushing to fast to
the desired positions.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-layoutAlgorithm-gravitationalConstant
title: gravitationalConstant
description:
Gravitational const used in the barycenter force of the
algorithm.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-layoutAlgorithm-initialPositionRadius
title: initialPositionRadius
description:
When `initialPositions` are set to 'circle',
`initialPositionRadius` is a distance from the center of circle,
in which nodes are created.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-layoutAlgorithm-initialPositions
title: initialPositions
description:
Initial layout algorithm for positioning nodes. Can be one of
built-in options ("circle", "random") or a function where
positions should be set on each node (`this.nodes`) as
`node.plotX` and `node.plotY`

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-layoutAlgorithm-integration
title: integration
description:
Integration type. Available options are `'euler'` and `'verlet'`.
Integration determines how forces are applied on particles. In
Euler integration, force is applied direct as
`newPosition += velocity;`.
In Verlet integration, new position is based on a previous
position without velocity:
`newPosition += previousPosition - newPosition`.

Note that different integrations give different results as forces
are different.

In Highcharts v7.0.x only `'euler'` integration was supported.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-layoutAlgorithm-linkLength
title: linkLength
description:
Ideal length (px) of the link between two nodes. When not
defined, length is calculated as:
`Math.pow(availableWidth * availableHeight / nodesLength, 0.4);`

Note: Because of the algorithm specification, length of each link
might be not exactly as specified.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-layoutAlgorithm-maxIterations
title: maxIterations
description:
Max number of iterations before algorithm will stop. In general,
algorithm should find positions sooner, but when rendering huge
number of nodes, it is recommended to increase this value as
finding perfect graph positions can require more time.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-layoutAlgorithm-maxSpeed
title: maxSpeed
description:
Verlet integration only.
Max speed that node can get in one iteration. In terms of
simulation, it's a maximum translation (in pixels) that node can
move (in both, x and y, dimensions). While `friction` is applied
on all nodes, max speed is applied only for nodes that move very
fast, for example small or disconnected ones.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-layoutAlgorithm-repulsiveForce
title: repulsiveForce
description:
Repulsive force applied on a node. Passed are two arguments:
- `d` - which is current distance between two nodes
- `k` - which is desired distance between two nodes

In `verlet` integration, defaults to:
`function (d, k) { return (k - d) / d * (k > d ? 1 : 0) }`

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-layoutAlgorithm-theta
title: theta
description:
Barnes-Hut approximation only.
Determines when distance between cell and node is small enough
to calculate forces. Value of `theta` is compared directly with
quotient `s / d`, where `s` is the size of the cell, and `d` is
distance between center of cell's mass and currently compared
node.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-layoutAlgorithm-type
title: type
description: Type of the algorithm used when positioning nodes.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-link
title: link
description: Link style options

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-link-color
title: color
description: Color of the link between two nodes.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-link-dashStyle
title: dashStyle
description: A name for the dash style to use for links.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-link-opacity
title: opacity
description: Opacity of the link between two nodes.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-link-width
title: width
description: Width (px) of the link between two nodes.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-marker-states-inactive
title: inactive
description:
The opposite state of a hover for a single point node.
Applied to all not connected nodes to the hovered one.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-marker-states-inactive-animation
title: animation
description: Animation when not hovering over the node.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-marker-states-inactive-opacity
title: opacity
description: Opacity of inactive markers.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-states-inactive
title: inactive
description:
The opposite state of a hover for a single point link. Applied
to all links that are not coming from the hovered node.

name: plotOptions-networkgraph-states-inactive-animation
title: animation
description: Animation when not hovering over the node.

name: plotOptions-organization
title: organization

name: plotOptions-organization-borderColor
title: borderColor
description: The border color of the node cards.

name: plotOptions-organization-borderRadius
title: borderRadius
description: The border radius of the node cards.

name: plotOptions-organization-dataLabels-nodeFormatter
title: nodeFormatter
description:
A callback for defining the format for _nodes_ in the
organization chart. The `nodeFormat` option takes precedence
over `nodeFormatter`.

In an organization chart, the `nodeFormatter` is a quite complex
function of the available options, striving for a good default
layout of cards with or without images. In organization chart,
the data labels come with `useHTML` set to true, meaning they
will be rendered as true HTML above the SVG.

name: plotOptions-organization-hangingIndent
title: hangingIndent
description:
The indentation in pixels of hanging nodes, nodes which parent has
[layout](#series.organization.nodes.layout) set to `hanging`.

name: plotOptions-organization-hangingIndentTranslation
title: hangingIndentTranslation
description:
Defines the indentation of a `hanging` layout parent's children.
Possible options:

- `inherit` (default): Only the first child adds the indentation,
children of a child with indentation inherit the indentation.
- `cumulative`: All children of a child with indentation add its
own indent. The option may cause overlapping of nodes.
Then use `shrink` option:
- `shrink`: Nodes shrink by the
[hangingIndent](#plotOptions.organization.hangingIndent)
value until they reach the
[minNodeLength](#plotOptions.organization.minNodeLength).

name: plotOptions-organization-hangingSide
title: hangingSide
description:
Whether links connecting hanging nodes should be drawn on the left
or right side. Useful for RTL layouts.
**Note:** Only effects inverted charts (vertical layout).

name: plotOptions-organization-link
title: link
description: Link Styling options

name: plotOptions-organization-link-color
title: color
description: The color of the links between nodes.

name: plotOptions-organization-link-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: The line width of the links connecting nodes, in pixels.

name: plotOptions-organization-link-radius
title: radius
description:
Radius for the rounded corners of the links between nodes.
Works for the `orthogonal` link type.

name: plotOptions-organization-link-type
title: type
description: Type of the link shape.

name: plotOptions-organization-minNodeLength
title: minNodeLength
description:
In a horizontal chart, the minimum width of the **hanging** nodes
only, in pixels. In a vertical chart, the minimum height of the
**hanging** nodes only, in pixels too.

Note: Used only when
[hangingIndentTranslation](#plotOptions.organization.hangingIndentTranslation)
is set to `shrink`.

name: plotOptions-organization-nodeWidth
title: nodeWidth
description:
In a horizontal chart, the width of the nodes in pixels. Note that
most organization charts are inverted (vertical), so the name of this
option is counterintuitive.

name: plotOptions-packedbubble
title: packedbubble

name: plotOptions-packedbubble-dataLabels-format
title: format
description:
The
[format string](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting)
specifying what to show for _node_ in the networkgraph. In v7.0
defaults to `{key}`, since v7.1 defaults to `undefined` and
`formatter` is used instead.

name: plotOptions-packedbubble-dataLabels-formatter
title: formatter
description:
Callback JavaScript function to format the data label for a node.
Note that if a `format` is defined, the format takes precedence
and the formatter is ignored.

name: plotOptions-packedbubble-dataLabels-parentNodeTextPath-attributes
title: attributes
description: Presentation attributes for the text path.

name: plotOptions-packedbubble-dataLabels-parentNodeTextPath-enabled
title: enabled
description:
Enable or disable `textPath` option for link's or marker's
data labels.

name: plotOptions-packedbubble-dataLabels-textPath
title: textPath
description:
Options for a _node_ label text which should follow marker's
shape.

**Note:** Only SVG-based renderer supports this option.

name: plotOptions-packedbubble-draggable
title: draggable
description:
Flag to determine if nodes are draggable or not. Available for
graph with useSimulation set to true only.

name: plotOptions-packedbubble-layoutAlgorithm
title: layoutAlgorithm
description:
Options for layout algorithm when simulation is enabled. Inside there
are options to change the speed, padding, initial bubbles positions
and more.

name: plotOptions-packedbubble-layoutAlgorithm-bubblePadding
title: bubblePadding
description:
The distance between two bubbles, when the algorithm starts to
treat two bubbles as overlapping. The `bubblePadding` is also the
expected distance between all the bubbles on simulation end.

name: plotOptions-packedbubble-layoutAlgorithm-dragBetweenSeries
title: dragBetweenSeries
description:
In case of split series, this option allows user to drag and
drop points between series, for changing point related series.

name: plotOptions-packedbubble-layoutAlgorithm-initialPositions
title: initialPositions
description:
Initial layout algorithm for positioning nodes. Can be one of
the built-in options ("circle", "random") or a function where
positions should be set on each node (`this.nodes`) as
`node.plotX` and `node.plotY`.

name: plotOptions-packedbubble-layoutAlgorithm-maxSpeed
title: maxSpeed
description:
Max speed that node can get in one iteration. In terms of
simulation, it's a maximum translation (in pixels) that a node
can move (in both, x and y, dimensions). While `friction` is
applied on all nodes, max speed is applied only for nodes that
move very fast, for example small or disconnected ones.

name: plotOptions-packedbubble-layoutAlgorithm-parentNodeLimit
title: parentNodeLimit
description:
Whether bubbles should interact with their parentNode to keep
them inside.

name: plotOptions-packedbubble-layoutAlgorithm-parentNodeOptions
title: parentNodeOptions
description: Layout algorithm options for parent nodes.

name: plotOptions-packedbubble-layoutAlgorithm-parentNodeOptions-marker
title: marker
description:
Styling options for parentNodes markers. Similar to
line.marker options.

name: plotOptions-packedbubble-layoutAlgorithm-seriesInteraction
title: seriesInteraction
description:
Whether series should interact with each other or not. When
`parentNodeLimit` is set to true, thi option should be set to
false to avoid sticking points in wrong series parentNode.

name: plotOptions-packedbubble-layoutAlgorithm-splitSeries
title: splitSeries
description:
Whether to split series into individual groups or to mix all
series together.

name: plotOptions-packedbubble-maxSize
title: maxSize
description:
Maximum bubble size. Bubbles will automatically size between the
`minSize` and `maxSize` to reflect the value of each bubble.
Can be either pixels (when no unit is given), or a percentage of
the smallest one of the plot width and height, divided by the square
root of total number of points.

name: plotOptions-packedbubble-minSize
title: minSize
description:
Minimum bubble size. Bubbles will automatically size between the
`minSize` and `maxSize` to reflect the value of each bubble.
Can be either pixels (when no unit is given), or a percentage of
the smallest one of the plot width and height, divided by the square
root of total number of points.

name: plotOptions-packedbubble-parentNode
title: parentNode
description: Series options for parent nodes.

name: plotOptions-packedbubble-parentNode-allowPointSelect
title: allowPointSelect
description:
Allow this series' parent nodes to be selected
by clicking on the graph.

name: plotOptions-packedbubble-useSimulation
title: useSimulation
description:
An option is giving a possibility to choose between using simulation
for calculating bubble positions. These reflects in both animation
and final position of bubbles. Simulation is also adding options to
the series graph based on used layout. In case of big data sets, with
any performance issues, it is possible to disable animation and pack
bubble in a simple circular way.

name: plotOptions-pareto
title: pareto

name: plotOptions-pareto-zIndex
title: zIndex
description: Higher zIndex than column series to draw line above shapes.

name: plotOptions-pictorial
title: pictorial

name: plotOptions-pie
title: pie

name: plotOptions-pie-borderColor
title: borderColor
description:
The color of the border surrounding each slice. When `null`, the
border takes the same color as the slice fill. This can be used
together with a `borderWidth` to fill drawing gaps created by
antialiasing artifacts in border-less pies.

In styled mode, the border stroke is given in the `.highcharts-point`
class.

name: plotOptions-pie-borderRadius
title: borderRadius
description:
The corner radius of the border surrounding each slice. A number
signifies pixels. A percentage string, like for example `50%`, signifies
a size relative to the radius and the inner radius.

name: plotOptions-pie-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description:
The width of the border surrounding each slice.

When setting the border width to 0, there may be small gaps between
the slices due to SVG antialiasing artifacts. To work around this,
keep the border width at 0.5 or 1, but set the `borderColor` to
`null` instead.

In styled mode, the border stroke width is given in the
`.highcharts-point` class.

name: plotOptions-pie-center
title: center
description:
The center of the pie chart relative to the plot area. Can be
percentages or pixel values. The default behavior (as of 3.0) is to
center the pie so that all slices and data labels are within the plot
area. As a consequence, the pie may actually jump around in a chart
with dynamic values, as the data labels move. In that case, the
center should be explicitly set, for example to `["50%", "50%"]`.

name: plotOptions-pie-color
title: color
description:
The color of the pie series. A pie series is represented as an empty
circle if the total sum of its values is 0. Use this property to
define the color of its border.

In styled mode, the color can be defined by the
[colorIndex](#plotOptions.series.colorIndex) option. Also, the series
color can be set with the `.highcharts-series`,
`.highcharts-color-{n}`, `.highcharts-{type}-series` or
`.highcharts-series-{n}` class, or individual classes given by the
`className` option.

name: plotOptions-pie-colors
title: colors
description:
A series specific or series type specific color set to use instead
of the global [colors](#colors).

name: plotOptions-pie-dataLabels-alignTo
title: alignTo
description:
Alignment method for data labels. Possible values are:

- `plotEdges`: Each label touches the nearest vertical edge of
  the plot area.

- `connectors`: Connectors have the same x position and the
  widest label of each half (left & right) touches the nearest
  vertical edge of the plot area.

name: plotOptions-pie-dataLabels-connectorColor
title: connectorColor
description:
The color of the line connecting the data label to the pie slice.
The default color is the same as the point's color.

In styled mode, the connector stroke is given in the
`.highcharts-data-label-connector` class.

name: plotOptions-pie-dataLabels-connectorPadding
title: connectorPadding
description:
The distance from the data label to the connector. Note that
data labels also have a default `padding`, so in order for the
connector to touch the text, the `padding` must also be 0.

name: plotOptions-pie-dataLabels-connectorShape
title: connectorShape
description:
Specifies the method that is used to generate the connector path.
Highcharts provides 3 built-in connector shapes: `'crookedLine'`
(default since v11), `'fixedOffset'` and `'straight'`.

Users can provide their own method by passing a function instead of a
string. Three arguments are passed to the callback:

- An object that holds the information about the coordinates of the
  label (`x` & `y` properties) and how the label is located in
  relation to the pie (`alignment` property). `alignment` can by one
  of the following: `'left'` (pie on the left side of the data
  label), `'right'` (pie on the right side of the data label) or
  `'center'` (data label overlaps the pie).

- An object that holds the information about the position of the
  connector. Its `touchingSliceAt` property tells the position of
  the place where the connector touches the slice.

- Data label options

The function has to return an SVG path definition in array form (see
the example).

name: plotOptions-pie-dataLabels-connectorWidth
title: connectorWidth
description:
The width of the line connecting the data label to the pie slice.

In styled mode, the connector stroke width is given in the
`.highcharts-data-label-connector` class.

name: plotOptions-pie-dataLabels-crookDistance
title: crookDistance
description:
Works only if `connectorShape` is `'crookedLine'`. It defines how
far from the vertical plot edge the connector path should be
crooked. With the default, `undefined`, the crook is placed so that
the horizontal line from the label intersects with the radial line
extending through the center of the pie slice.

name: plotOptions-pie-dataLabels-distance
title: distance
description:
The distance of the data label from the pie's edge. Negative
numbers put the data label on top of the pie slices. Can also be
defined as a percentage of pie's radius. Connectors are only
shown for data labels outside the pie.

name: plotOptions-pie-dataLabels-format
title: format
description:
A
[format string](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting)
for the data label. Available variables are the same as for
`formatter`.

name: plotOptions-pie-dataLabels-formatter
title: formatter
description:
Callback JavaScript function to format the data label. Note that
if a `format` is defined, the format takes precedence and the
formatter is ignored.

name: plotOptions-pie-dataLabels-softConnector
title: softConnector
description:
Whether to render the connector as a soft arc or a line with a sharp
break. Works only if `connectorShape` equals to `fixedOffset`.

name: plotOptions-pie-depth
title: depth
description: The thickness of a 3D pie.

name: plotOptions-pie-endAngle
title: endAngle
description:
The end angle of the pie in degrees where 0 is top and 90 is right.
Defaults to `startAngle` plus 360.

name: plotOptions-pie-events-checkboxClick
title: checkboxClick
description:
Fires when the checkbox next to the point name in the legend is
clicked. One parameter, event, is passed to the function. The state
of the checkbox is found by event.checked. The checked item is found
by event.item. Return false to prevent the default action which is to
toggle the select state of the series.

name: plotOptions-pie-fillColor
title: fillColor
description:
If the total sum of the pie's values is 0, the series is represented
as an empty circle . The `fillColor` option defines the color of that
circle. Use [pie.borderWidth](#plotOptions.pie.borderWidth) to set
the border thickness.

name: plotOptions-pie-ignoreHiddenPoint
title: ignoreHiddenPoint
description:
Equivalent to [chart.ignoreHiddenSeries](#chart.ignoreHiddenSeries),
this option tells whether the series shall be redrawn as if the
hidden point were `null`.

The default value changed from `false` to `true` with Highcharts
3.0.

name: plotOptions-pie-innerSize
title: innerSize
description:
The size of the inner diameter for the pie. A size greater than 0
renders a donut chart. Can be a percentage or pixel value.
Percentages are relative to the pie size. Pixel values are given as
integers. Setting overridden by thickness.


Note: in Highcharts < 4.1.2, the percentage was relative to the plot
area, not the pie size.

name: plotOptions-pie-minSize
title: minSize

name: plotOptions-pie-showInLegend
title: showInLegend
description:
Whether to display this particular series or series type in the
legend. Since 2.1, pies are not shown in the legend by default.

name: plotOptions-pie-size
title: size
description:
The diameter of the pie relative to the plot area. Can be a
percentage or pixel value. Pixel values are given as integers. The
default behavior (as of 3.0) is to scale to the plot area and give
room for data labels within the plot area.
[slicedOffset](#plotOptions.pie.slicedOffset) is also included in the
default size calculation. As a consequence, the size of the pie may
vary when points are updated and data labels more around. In that
case it is best to set a fixed value, for example `"75%"`.

name: plotOptions-pie-slicedOffset
title: slicedOffset
description:
If a point is sliced, moved out from the center, how many pixels
should it be moved?.

name: plotOptions-pie-startAngle
title: startAngle
description:
The start angle of the pie slices in degrees where 0 is top and 90
right.

name: plotOptions-pie-states-hover-brightness
title: brightness
description:
How much to brighten the point on interaction.

In styled mode, the hover brightness is by default replaced
by a fill-opacity given in the `.highcharts-point-hover`
class.

name: plotOptions-pie-stickyTracking
title: stickyTracking
description:
Sticky tracking of mouse events. When true, the `mouseOut` event
on a series isn't triggered until the mouse moves over another
series, or out of the plot area. When false, the `mouseOut` event on
a series is triggered when the mouse leaves the area around the
series'  graph or markers. This also implies the tooltip. When
`stickyTracking` is false and `tooltip.shared` is false, the tooltip
will be hidden when moving the mouse between series.

name: plotOptions-pie-thickness
title: thickness
description:
Thickness describing the ring size for a donut type chart,
overriding [innerSize](#plotOptions.pie.innerSize).

name: plotOptions-polygon
title: polygon

name: plotOptions-polygon-fillOpacity
title: fillOpacity
description:
Fill opacity for the polygon. When you set an explicit `fillColor`,
the `fillOpacity` is not applied. Instead, you should define the
opacity in the `fillColor` with an rgba color definition.

In styled mode, the fill opacity can be set with the
`.highcharts-area` class name.

name: plotOptions-pyramid
title: pyramid

name: plotOptions-pyramid3d
title: pyramid3d

name: plotOptions-pyramid3d-reversed
title: reversed
description:
A reversed pyramid3d is funnel3d, but the latter supports neck
related options: neckHeight and neckWidth

name: plotOptions-sankey
title: sankey

name: plotOptions-sankey-curveFactor
title: curveFactor
description:
Higher numbers makes the links in a sankey diagram or dependency
wheel render more curved. A `curveFactor` of 0 makes the lines
straight.

name: plotOptions-sankey-dataLabels
title: dataLabels
description:
Options for the data labels appearing on top of the nodes and links.
For sankey charts, data labels are visible for the nodes by default,
but hidden for links. This is controlled by modifying the
`nodeFormat`, and the `format` that applies to links and is an empty
string by default.

name: plotOptions-sankey-dataLabels-nodeFormat
title: nodeFormat
description:
The
[format string](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting)
specifying what to show for _nodes_ in the sankey diagram. By
default the `nodeFormatter` returns `{point.name}`.

name: plotOptions-sankey-dataLabels-nodeFormatter
title: nodeFormatter
description:
Callback to format data labels for _nodes_ in the sankey diagram.
The `nodeFormat` option takes precedence over the
`nodeFormatter`.

name: plotOptions-sankey-levels
title: levels
description:
Set options on specific levels. Takes precedence over series options,
but not node and link options.

name: plotOptions-sankey-levels-borderColor
title: borderColor
description: Can set `borderColor` on all nodes which lay on the same level.

name: plotOptions-sankey-levels-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description: Can set `borderWidth` on all nodes which lay on the same level.

name: plotOptions-sankey-levels-color
title: color
description: Can set `color` on all nodes which lay on the same level.

name: plotOptions-sankey-levels-colorByPoint
title: colorByPoint
description: Can set `colorByPoint` on all nodes which lay on the same level.

name: plotOptions-sankey-levels-dataLabels
title: dataLabels
description: Can set `dataLabels` on all points which lay on the same level.

name: plotOptions-sankey-levels-level
title: level
description:
Decides which level takes effect from the options set in the levels
object.

name: plotOptions-sankey-levels-linkOpacity
title: linkOpacity
description: Can set `linkOpacity` on all points which lay on the same level.

name: plotOptions-sankey-levels-states
title: states
description: Can set `states` on all nodes and points which lay on the same level.

name: plotOptions-sankey-linkColorMode
title: linkColorMode
description:
Determines color mode for sankey links. Available options:

- `from` color of the sankey link will be the same as the 'from node'

- `gradient` color of the sankey link will be set to gradient between
colors of 'from node' and 'to node'

- `to` color of the sankey link will be same as the 'to node'.

name: plotOptions-sankey-linkOpacity
title: linkOpacity
description: Opacity for the links between nodes in the sankey diagram.

name: plotOptions-sankey-minLinkWidth
title: minLinkWidth
description:
The minimal width for a line of a sankey. By default,
0 values are not shown.

name: plotOptions-sankey-nodeAlignment
title: nodeAlignment
description:
Determines which side of the chart the nodes are to be aligned to. When
the chart is inverted, `top` aligns to the left and `bottom` to the
right.

name: plotOptions-sankey-nodeDistance
title: nodeDistance
description:
The distance between nodes in a sankey diagram in the longitudinal
direction. The longitudinal direction means the direction that the chart
flows - in a horizontal chart the distance is horizontal, in an inverted
chart (vertical), the distance is vertical.

If a number is given, it denotes pixels. If a percentage string is given,
the distance is a percentage of the rendered node width. A `nodeDistance`
of `100%` will render equal widths for the nodes and the gaps between
them.

This option applies only when the `nodeWidth` option is `auto`, making
the node width respond to the number of columns.

name: plotOptions-sankey-nodePadding
title: nodePadding
description:
The padding between nodes in a sankey diagram or dependency wheel, in
pixels. For sankey charts, this applies to the nodes of the same column,
so vertical distance by default, or horizontal distance in an inverted
(vertical) sankey.

If the number of nodes is so great that it is impossible to lay them out
within the plot area with the given `nodePadding`, they will be rendered
with a smaller padding as a strategy to avoid overflow.

name: plotOptions-sankey-nodeWidth
title: nodeWidth
description:
The pixel width of each node in a sankey diagram or dependency wheel, or
the height in case the chart is inverted.

Can be a number or a percentage string.

Sankey series also support setting it to `auto`. With this setting, the
nodes are sized to fill up the plot area in the longitudinal direction,
regardless of the number of levels.

name: plotOptions-sankey-opacity
title: opacity
description: Opacity for the nodes in the sankey diagram.

name: plotOptions-sankey-states-hover-linkOpacity
title: linkOpacity
description:
Opacity for the links between nodes in the sankey diagram in
hover mode.

name: plotOptions-sankey-states-hover-opacity
title: opacity
description: Opacity for the nodes in the sankey diagram in hover mode.

name: plotOptions-sankey-states-inactive
title: inactive
description: The opposite state of a hover for a single point node/link.

name: plotOptions-sankey-states-inactive-linkOpacity
title: linkOpacity
description:
Opacity for the links between nodes in the sankey diagram in
inactive mode.

name: plotOptions-sankey-states-inactive-opacity
title: opacity
description: Opacity of the nodes in the sankey diagram in inactive mode.

name: plotOptions-sankey-tooltip-followPointer
title: followPointer
description:
Whether the tooltip should follow the pointer or stay fixed on
the item.

name: plotOptions-sankey-tooltip-nodeFormat
title: nodeFormat
description:
The
[format string](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting)
specifying what to show for _nodes_ in tooltip of a diagram
series, as opposed to links.

name: plotOptions-sankey-tooltip-nodeFormatter
title: nodeFormatter
description:
A callback for defining the format for _nodes_ in the chart's
tooltip, as opposed to links.

name: plotOptions-scatter
title: scatter

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster
title: cluster
description:
Options for marker clusters, the concept of sampling the data
values into larger blocks in order to ease readability and
increase performance of the JavaScript charts.

Note: marker clusters module is not working with `boost`
and `draggable-points` modules.

The marker clusters feature requires the marker-clusters.js
file to be loaded, found in the modules directory of the download
package, or online at [code.highcharts.com/modules/marker-clusters.js](code.highcharts.com/modules/marker-clusters.js).

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-allowOverlap
title: allowOverlap
description:
When set to `false` prevent cluster overlapping - this option
works only when `layoutAlgorithm.type = "grid"`.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-animation
title: animation
description: Options for the cluster marker animation.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-dataLabels
title: dataLabels
description: Options for the cluster data labels.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-drillToCluster
title: drillToCluster
description: Zoom the plot area to the cluster points range when a cluster is clicked.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-enabled
title: enabled
description: Whether to enable the marker-clusters module.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-events-drillToCluster
title: drillToCluster
description:
Fires when the cluster point is clicked and `drillToCluster` is enabled.
One parameter, `event`, is passed to the function. The default action
is to zoom to the cluster points range. This can be prevented
by calling `event.preventDefault()`.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-layoutAlgorithm
title: layoutAlgorithm
description:
Options for layout algorithm. Inside there
are options to change the type of the algorithm, gridSize,
distance or iterations.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-layoutAlgorithm-distance
title: distance
description:
When `type` is set to `kmeans`,
`distance` is a maximum distance between point and cluster center
so that this point will be inside the cluster. The distance
is either a number defining pixels or a percentage
defining a percentage of the plot area width.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-layoutAlgorithm-gridSize
title: gridSize
description:
When `type` is set to the `grid`,
`gridSize` is a size of a grid square element either as a number
defining pixels, or a percentage defining a percentage
of the plot area width.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-layoutAlgorithm-iterations
title: iterations
description:
When `type` is set to `kmeans`,
`iterations` are the number of iterations that this algorithm will be
repeated to find clusters positions.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-layoutAlgorithm-kmeansThreshold
title: kmeansThreshold
description:
When `type` is set to `undefined` and there are more visible points
than the kmeansThreshold the `grid` algorithm is used to find
clusters, otherwise `kmeans`. It ensures good performance on
large datasets and better clusters arrangement after the zoom.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-layoutAlgorithm-type
title: type
description:
Type of the algorithm used to combine points into a cluster. There are three available algorithms: 1) `grid` - grid-based clustering technique. Points are assigned to squares of set size depending on their position on the plot area. Points inside the grid square are combined into a cluster. The grid size can be controlled by `gridSize` property (grid size changes at certain zoom levels). 2) `kmeans` - based on K-Means clustering technique. In the first step, points are divided using the grid method (distance property is a grid size) to find the initial amount of clusters. Next, each point is classified by computing the distance between each cluster center and that point. When the closest cluster distance is lower than distance property set by a user the point is added to this cluster otherwise is classified as `noise`. The algorithm is repeated until each cluster center not change its previous position more than one pixel. This technique is more accurate but also more time consuming than the `grid` algorithm, especially for big datasets. 3) `optimizedKmeans` - based on K-Means clustering technique. This algorithm uses k-means algorithm only on the chart initialization or when chart extremes have greater range than on initialization. When a chart is redrawn the algorithm checks only clustered points distance from the cluster center and rebuild it when the point is spaced enough to be outside the cluster. It provides performance improvement and more stable clusters position yet can be used rather on small and sparse datasets. By default, the algorithm depends on visible quantity of points and `kmeansThreshold`. When there are more visible points than the `kmeansThreshold` the `grid` algorithm is used, otherwise `kmeans`. The custom clustering algorithm can be added by assigning a callback function as the type property. This function takes an array of `processedXData`, `processedYData`, `processedXData` indexes and `layoutAlgorithm` options as arguments and should return an object with grouped data. The algorithm should return an object like that: 
{
 clusterId1: [{
     x: 573,
     y: 285,
     index: 1 // point index in the data array
 }, {
     x: 521,
     y: 197,
     index: 2
 }],
 clusterId2: [{
     ...
 }]
 ...
}
`clusterId` (example above - unique id of a cluster or noise) is an array of points belonging to a cluster. If the array has only one point or fewer points than set in `cluster.minimumClusterSize` it won't be combined into a cluster.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-marker
title: marker
description: Options for the cluster marker.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-minimumClusterSize
title: minimumClusterSize
description:
The minimum amount of points to be combined into a cluster.
This value has to be greater or equal to 2.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-states-hover-fillColor
title: fillColor
description:
The fill color of the cluster marker in hover state. When
`undefined`, the series' or point's fillColor for normal
state is used.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-zones
title: zones
description:
An array defining zones within marker clusters.

In styled mode, the color zones are styled with the
`.highcharts-cluster-zone-{n}` class, or custom
classed from the `className`
option.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-zones-className
title: className
description: Styled mode only. A custom class name for the zone.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-zones-from
title: from
description: The value where the zone starts.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-zones-marker
title: marker
description: Settings for the cluster marker belonging to the zone.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-zones-to
title: to
description: The value where the zone ends.

name: plotOptions-scatter-jitter
title: jitter
description:
Apply a jitter effect for the rendered markers. When plotting
discrete values, a little random noise may help telling the points
apart. The jitter setting applies a random displacement of up to `n`
axis units in either direction. So for example on a horizontal X
axis, setting the `jitter.x` to 0.24 will render the point in a
random position between 0.24 units to the left and 0.24 units to the
right of the true axis position. On a category axis, setting it to
0.5 will fill up the bin and make the data appear continuous.

When rendered on top of a box plot or a column series, a jitter value
of 0.24 will correspond to the underlying series' default
[groupPadding](https://api.highcharts.com/highcharts/plotOptions.column.groupPadding)
and [pointPadding](https://api.highcharts.com/highcharts/plotOptions.column.pointPadding)
settings.

**Note:** With boost mode enabled, the jitter effect is not supported.

name: plotOptions-scatter-jitter-x
title: x
description: The maximal X offset for the random jitter effect.

name: plotOptions-scatter-jitter-y
title: y
description: The maximal Y offset for the random jitter effect.

name: plotOptions-scatter-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: The width of the line connecting the data points.

name: plotOptions-scatter-stickyTracking
title: stickyTracking
description:
Sticky tracking of mouse events. When true, the `mouseOut` event
on a series isn't triggered until the mouse moves over another
series, or out of the plot area. When false, the `mouseOut` event on
a series is triggered when the mouse leaves the area around the
series' graph or markers. This also implies the tooltip. When
`stickyTracking` is false and `tooltip.shared` is false, the tooltip
will be hidden when moving the mouse between series.

name: plotOptions-scatter-tooltip
title: tooltip
description:
A configuration object for the tooltip rendering of each single
series. Properties are inherited from [tooltip](#tooltip).
Overridable properties are `headerFormat`, `pointFormat`,
`yDecimals`, `xDateFormat`, `yPrefix` and `ySuffix`. Unlike other
series, in a scatter plot the series.name by default shows in the
headerFormat and point.x and point.y in the pointFormat.

name: plotOptions-scatter3d
title: scatter3d

name: plotOptions-series
title: series

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility
title: accessibility
description: Accessibility options for a series.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-description
title: description
description: Provide a description of the series, announced to screen readers.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-descriptionFormat
title: descriptionFormat
description:
Format to use for describing the data series group to assistive
technology - including screen readers.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable/disable accessibility functionality for a specific series.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-exposeAsGroupOnly
title: exposeAsGroupOnly
description: Expose only the series element to screen readers, not its points.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-keyboardNavigation
title: keyboardNavigation
description: Keyboard navigation for a series

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-keyboardNavigation-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable/disable keyboard navigation support for a specific series.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-point
title: point
description: Point accessibility options for a series.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-point-dateFormat
title: dateFormat
description:
Date format to use for points on datetime axes when describing
them to screen reader users.

Defaults to the same format as in tooltip.

For an overview of the replacement codes, see
[dateFormat](/class-reference/Highcharts.Time#dateFormat).

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-point-dateFormatter
title: dateFormatter
description:
Formatter function to determine the date/time format used with
points on datetime axes when describing them to screen reader
users. Receives one argument, `point`, referring to the point
to describe. Should return a date format string compatible with
[dateFormat](/class-reference/Highcharts.Time#dateFormat).

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-point-describeNull
title: describeNull
description:
Whether or not to describe points with the value `null` to
assistive technology, such as screen readers.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-point-descriptionFormat
title: descriptionFormat
description:
A [format string](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting)
to use instead of the default for point descriptions.

The context of the format string is the point instance.

As opposed to [accessibility.point.valueDescriptionFormat](#accessibility.point.valueDescriptionFormat),
this option replaces the whole description.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-point-descriptionFormatter
title: descriptionFormatter
description:
Formatter function to use instead of the default for point
descriptions. Same as `accessibility.point.descriptionFormatter`, but
applies to a series instead of the whole chart.

Note: Prefer using [accessibility.point.valueDescriptionFormat](#plotOptions.series.accessibility.point.valueDescriptionFormat)
instead if possible, as default functionality such as describing
annotations will be preserved.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-point-valueDecimals
title: valueDecimals
