description:
Decimals to use for the values in the point descriptions. Uses
[tooltip.valueDecimals](#tooltip.valueDecimals) if not defined.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-point-valueDescriptionFormat
title: valueDescriptionFormat
description:
Format to use for describing the values of data points
to assistive technology - including screen readers.
The point context is available as `{point}`.

Other available context variables include `{index}`, `{value}`, and `{xDescription}`.

Additionally, the series name, annotation info, and
description added in `point.accessibility.description`
is added by default if relevant. To override this, use the
[accessibility.point.descriptionFormatter](#accessibility.point.descriptionFormatter)
option.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-point-valuePrefix
title: valuePrefix
description:
Prefix to add to the values in the point descriptions. Uses
[tooltip.valuePrefix](#tooltip.valuePrefix) if not defined.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-point-valueSuffix
title: valueSuffix
description:
Suffix to add to the values in the point descriptions. Uses
[tooltip.valueSuffix](#tooltip.valueSuffix) if not defined.

name: plotOptions-series-allowPointSelect
title: allowPointSelect
description:
Allow this series' points to be selected by clicking on the graphic
(columns, point markers, pie slices, map areas etc).

The selected points can be handled by point select and unselect
events, or collectively by the [getSelectedPoints](/class-reference/Highcharts.Chart#getSelectedPoints) function.

And alternative way of selecting points is through dragging.

name: plotOptions-series-animation
title: animation
description:
Enable or disable the initial animation when a series is displayed.
The animation can also be set as a configuration object. Please
note that this option only applies to the initial animation of the
series itself. For other animations, see [chart.animation](#chart.animation) and the animation parameter under the API methods.
The following properties are supported:

- `defer`: The animation delay time in milliseconds.

- `duration`: The duration of the animation in milliseconds. (Defaults to
  `1000`)

- `easing`: Can be a string reference to an easing function set on
  the `Math` object or a function. See the _Custom easing function_
  demo below. (Defaults to `easeInOutSine`)

Due to poor performance, animation is disabled in old IE browsers
for several chart types.

name: plotOptions-series-animationLimit
title: animationLimit
description:
For some series, there is a limit that shuts down animation
by default when the total number of points in the chart is too high.
For example, for a column chart and its derivatives, animation does
not run if there is more than 250 points totally. To disable this
cap, set `animationLimit` to `Infinity`. This option works if animation
is fired on individual points, not on a group of points like e.g. during
the initial animation.

name: plotOptions-series-boostBlending
title: boostBlending
description: Sets the color blending in the boost module.

name: plotOptions-series-boostThreshold
title: boostThreshold
description:
Set the point threshold for when a series should enter boost mode.

Setting it to e.g. 2000 will cause the series to enter boost mode when there
are 2000 or more points in the series.

To disable boosting on the series, set the `boostThreshold` to 0. Setting it
to 1 will force boosting.

Note that the [cropThreshold](plotOptions.series.cropThreshold) also affects
this setting. When zooming in on a series that has fewer points than the
`cropThreshold`, all points are rendered although outside the visible plot
area, and the `boostThreshold` won't take effect.

name: plotOptions-series-className
title: className
description:
An additional class name to apply to the series' graphical elements.
This option does not replace default class names of the graphical
element. Changes to the series' color will also be reflected in a
chart's legend and tooltip.

name: plotOptions-series-clip
title: clip
description:
Disable this option to allow series rendering in the whole plotting
area.

**Note:** Clipping should be always enabled when
[chart.zoomType](#chart.zoomType) is set

name: plotOptions-series-color
title: color
description:
The main color of the series. In line type series it applies to the
line and the point markers unless otherwise specified. In bar type
series it applies to the bars unless a color is specified per point.
The default value is pulled from the `options.colors` array.

In styled mode, the color can be defined by the
[colorIndex](#plotOptions.series.colorIndex) option. Also, the series
color can be set with the `.highcharts-series`,
`.highcharts-color-{n}`, `.highcharts-{type}-series` or
`.highcharts-series-{n}` class, or individual classes given by the
`className` option.

name: plotOptions-series-colorAxis
title: colorAxis
description:
When using dual or multiple color axes, this number defines which
colorAxis the particular series is connected to. It refers to
either the
{@link #colorAxis.id|axis id}
or the index of the axis in the colorAxis array, with 0 being the
first. Set this option to false to prevent a series from connecting
to the default color axis.

Since v7.2.0 the option can also be an axis id or an axis index
instead of a boolean flag.

name: plotOptions-series-colorIndex
title: colorIndex
description:
Styled mode only. A specific color index to use for the series, so its
graphic representations are given the class name `highcharts-color-{n}`.

Since v11, CSS variables on the form `--highcharts-color-{n}` make
changing the color scheme very convenient.

name: plotOptions-series-colorKey
title: colorKey
description:
Determines what data value should be used to calculate point color
if `colorAxis` is used. Requires to set `min` and `max` if some
custom point property is used or if approximation for data grouping
is set to `'sum'`.

name: plotOptions-series-connectEnds
title: connectEnds
description:
Polar charts only. Whether to connect the ends of a line series
plot across the extremes.

name: plotOptions-series-connectNulls
title: connectNulls
description:
Whether to connect a graph line across null points, or render a gap
between the two points on either side of the null.

In stacked area chart, if `connectNulls` is set to true,
null points are interpreted as 0.

name: plotOptions-series-crisp
title: crisp
description:
When true, each point or column edge is rounded to its nearest pixel
in order to render sharp on screen. In some cases, when there are a
lot of densely packed columns, this leads to visible difference
in column widths or distance between columns. In these cases,
setting `crisp` to `false` may look better, even though each column
is rendered blurry.

name: plotOptions-series-cropThreshold
title: cropThreshold
description:
When the series contains less points than the crop threshold, all
points are drawn, even if the points fall outside the visible plot
area at the current zoom. The advantage of drawing all points
(including markers and columns), is that animation is performed on
updates. On the other hand, when the series contains more points than
the crop threshold, the series data is cropped to only contain points
that fall within the plot area. The advantage of cropping away
invisible points is to increase performance on large series.

name: plotOptions-series-cursor
title: cursor
description:
You can set the cursor to "pointer" if you have click events attached
to the series, to signal to the user that the points and lines can
be clicked.

In styled mode, the series cursor can be set with the same classes
as listed under [series.color](#plotOptions.series.color).

name: plotOptions-series-custom
title: custom
description:
A reserved subspace to store options and values for customized
functionality. Here you can add additional data for your own event
callbacks and formatter callbacks.

name: plotOptions-series-dashStyle
title: dashStyle
description:
Name of the dash style to use for the graph, or for some series types
the outline of each shape.

In styled mode, the
[stroke dash-array](https://jsfiddle.net/gh/get/library/pure/highcharts/highcharts/tree/master/samples/highcharts/css/series-dashstyle/)
can be set with the same classes as listed under
[series.color](#plotOptions.series.color).

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels
title: dataLabels
description:
Options for the series data labels, appearing next to each data point.

Since v6.2.0, multiple data labels can be applied to each single
point by defining them as an array of configs.

In styled mode, the data labels can be styled with the
`.highcharts-data-label-box` and `.highcharts-data-label` class names
([see example](https://www.highcharts.com/samples/highcharts/css/series-datalabels)).

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-align
title: align
description:
The alignment of the data label compared to the point. If `right`,
the right side of the label should be touching the point. For points
with an extent, like columns, the alignments also dictates how to
align it inside the box, as given with the
[inside](#plotOptions.column.dataLabels.inside) option. Can be one of
`left`, `center` or `right`.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-alignTo
title: alignTo
description:
Alignment method for data labels. If set to `plotEdges`, the labels
are aligned within the plot area in the direction of the y-axis. So
in a regular column chart, the labels are aligned vertically
according to the `verticalAlign` setting. In a bar chart, which is
inverted, the labels are aligned horizontally according to the
`align` setting. Applies to cartesian series only.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-allowOverlap
title: allowOverlap
description:
Whether to allow data labels to overlap. To make the labels less
sensitive for overlapping, the
[dataLabels.padding](#plotOptions.series.dataLabels.padding)
can be set to 0.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-animation
title: animation
description:
Enable or disable the initial animation when a series is displayed
for the `dataLabels`. The animation can also be set as a
configuration object. Please note that this option only applies to
the initial animation.

For other animations, see [chart.animation](#chart.animation) and the
animation parameter under the API methods. The following properties
are supported:

- `defer`: The animation delay time in milliseconds.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-animation-defer
title: defer
description:
The animation delay time in milliseconds. Set to `0` to render the
data labels immediately. As `undefined` inherits defer time from the
[series.animation.defer](#plotOptions.series.animation.defer).

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-backgroundColor
title: backgroundColor
description:
The background color or gradient for the data label. In addition to
regular colors, there are two special setting for this option:
- `auto` will set the background color the point's color.
- `contrast` will set it to a contrast against the text color, with
  an opacity allowing to see the underlying content. The contrast is
  great enough to ensure readability for the text according to
  accessibility standards.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-borderColor
title: borderColor
description:
The border color for the data label. Setting it to `auto` will use
the point's color. Defaults to `undefined`.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-borderRadius
title: borderRadius
description: The border radius in pixels for the data label.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description: The border width in pixels for the data label.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-className
title: className
description:
A class name for the data label. Particularly in styled mode,
this can be used to give each series' or point's data label
unique styling. In addition to this option, a default color class
name is added so that we can give the labels a contrast text
shadow.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-crop
title: crop
description:
Whether to hide data labels that are outside the plot area. By
default, the data label is moved inside the plot area according
to the
[overflow](#plotOptions.series.dataLabels.overflow)
option.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-defer
title: defer
description:
Whether to defer displaying the data labels until the initial
series animation has finished. Setting to `false` renders the
data label immediately. If set to `true` inherits the defer
time set in [plotOptions.series.animation](#plotOptions.series.animation).

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-distance
title: distance
description:
The distance of the data label from the data point. Note that the
`padding` setting also affects the rendered distance, but is not
visible unless the data label has a border or background.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable or disable the data labels.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-filter
title: filter
description:
A declarative filter to control of which data labels to display.
The declarative filter is designed for use when callback
functions are not available, like when the chart options require
a pure JSON structure or for use with graphical editors. For
programmatic control, use the `formatter` instead, and return
`undefined` to disable a single data label.

```js
filter: {
    property: 'percentage',
    operator: '>',
    value: 4
}
```

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-filter-operator
title: operator
description:
The operator to compare by. Can be one of `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`,
`==`, `===`, `!=` and `!==`.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-filter-property
title: property
description:
The point property to filter by. Point options are passed
directly to properties, additionally there are `y` value,
`percentage` and others listed under {@link Highcharts.Point}
members.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-filter-value
title: value
description: The value to compare against.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-format
title: format
description:
A
[format string](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting)
for the data label. Available variables are the same as for
`formatter`.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-formatter
title: formatter
description:
Callback JavaScript function to format the data label. Note that if a
`format` is defined, the format takes precedence and the formatter is
ignored.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-inside
title: inside
description:
For points with an extent, like columns or map areas, whether to
align the data label inside the box or to the actual value point.
Defaults to `false` in most cases, `true` in stacked columns.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-labelrank
title: labelrank
description:
The rank for this point's data label in case of collision. If two
data labels are about to overlap, only the one with the highest
`labelrank` will be drawn.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-nullFormat
title: nullFormat
description:
Format for points with the value of null. Works analogously to
[format](#plotOptions.series.dataLabels.format). `nullFormat` can
be applied only to series which support displaying null points.
`heatmap` and `tilemap` supports `nullFormat` by default while the
following series requires [#series.nullInteraction] set to `true`:
`line`, `spline`, `area`, `area-spline`, `column`, `bar`, and
`timeline`. Does not work with series that don't display null
points, like `pie`.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-nullFormatter
title: nullFormatter
description:
Callback JavaScript function that defines formatting for points
with the value of null. Works analogously to
[formatter](#plotOptions.series.dataLabels.formatter).
`nullFormatter` can be applied only to series which support
displaying null points. `heatmap` and `tilemap` supports
`nullFormatter` by default while the following series requires
(series.nullInteraction)[#series.nullInteraction]
set to `true`: `line`, `spline`, `area`, `area-spline`, `column`,
`bar`, and `timeline`. Does not work with series that don't display
null points, like `pie`.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-overflow
title: overflow
description:
How to handle data labels that flow outside the plot area. The
default is `"justify"`, which aligns them inside the plot area.
For columns and bars, this means it will be moved inside the bar.
To display data labels outside the plot area, set `crop` to
`false` and `overflow` to `"allow"`.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-padding
title: padding
description:
When either the `borderWidth` or the `backgroundColor` is set,
this is the padding within the box.

An array of numbers sets padding for the respective sides. An array
of two numbers repeats the values for the horizontal and vertical
sides.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-position
title: position
description:
Aligns data labels relative to points. If `center` alignment is
not possible, it defaults to `right`.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-rotation
title: rotation
description:
Text rotation in degrees. Note that due to a more complex
structure, backgrounds, borders and padding will be lost on a
rotated data label.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-shadow
title: shadow
description:
The shadow of the box. Works best with `borderWidth` or
`backgroundColor`. Since 2.3 the shadow can be an object
configuration containing `color`, `offsetX`, `offsetY`, `opacity`
and `width`.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-shape
title: shape
description:
The name of a symbol to use for the border around the label.
Symbols are predefined functions on the Renderer object.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-style
title: style
description:
Styles for the label. The default `color` setting is
`"contrast"`, which is a pseudo color that Highcharts picks up
and applies the maximum contrast to the underlying point item,
for example the bar in a bar chart.

The `textOutline` is a pseudo property that applies an outline of
the given width with the given color, which by default is the
maximum contrast to the text. So a bright text color will result
in a black text outline for maximum readability on a mixed
background. In some cases, especially with grayscale text, the
text outline doesn't work well, in which cases it can be disabled
by setting it to `"none"`. When `useHTML` is true, the
`textOutline` will not be picked up. In this, case, the same
effect can be achieved through the `text-shadow` CSS property. As a
complementary or alternative to the `textOutline`, a
`dataLabels.backgroundColor` can be used. It provides a more calm
impression and ensures readable text label, at the cost of a risk of
overshadowing the underlying chart elements.

For some series types, where each point has an extent, like for
example tree maps, the data label may overflow the point. There
are two strategies for handling overflow. By default, the text
will wrap to multiple lines. The other strategy is to set
`style.textOverflow` to `ellipsis`, which will keep the text on
one line plus it will break inside long words.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-textPath
title: textPath
description:
Options for a label text which should follow marker's shape.
Border and background are disabled for a label that follows a
path.

**Note:** Only SVG-based renderer supports this option. Setting
`useHTML` to true will disable this option.

Text path support is not bundled into `highcharts.js`, and requires the
`modules/textpath.js` file. However, it is included in the script files of
those series types that use it by default.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-textPath-attributes
title: attributes
description: Presentation attributes for the text path.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-textPath-enabled
title: enabled
description:
Enable or disable `textPath` option for link's or marker's data
labels.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-useHTML
title: useHTML
description:
Whether to
[use HTML](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting#html)
to render the labels.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-verticalAlign
title: verticalAlign
description:
The vertical alignment of a data label. Can be one of `top`,
`middle` or `bottom`. The default value depends on the data, for
instance in a column chart, the label is above positive values
and below negative values.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-x
title: x
description:
The x position offset of the label relative to the point in
pixels.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-y
title: y
description:
The y position offset of the label relative to the point in
pixels.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-zIndex
title: zIndex
description:
The z index of the data labels group. Does not apply below series
level options.

Use a `zIndex` of 6 to display it above the series,
or use a `zIndex` of 2 to display it behind the series.

name: plotOptions-series-dataMapping
title: dataMapping

name: plotOptions-series-dataSorting
title: dataSorting
description: Options for series data sorting.

name: plotOptions-series-dataSorting-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable or disable data sorting for the series. Use [xAxis.reversed](#xAxis.reversed) to change the sorting order.

name: plotOptions-series-dataSorting-matchByName
title: matchByName
description:
Whether to allow matching points by name in an update. If this option
is disabled, points will be matched by order.

name: plotOptions-series-dataSorting-sortKey
title: sortKey
description: Determines what data value should be used to sort by.

name: plotOptions-series-dataTable
title: dataTable
description:
Options for a specific series-level data table or an array of data
tables. The `dataTable` option can be either a configuration object or an
instance of the `DataTable` class. If a `DataTable` instance is passed,
it will be used directly. If a configuration object or an array is
passed, a new `DataTable` instance will be created based on the provided
configuration.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop
title: dragDrop
description:
The draggable-points module allows points to be moved around or modified in
the chart. In addition to the options mentioned under the `dragDrop` API
structure, the module fires three events,
[point.dragStart](plotOptions.series.point.events.dragStart),
[point.drag](plotOptions.series.point.events.drag) and
[point.drop](plotOptions.series.point.events.drop).

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragHandle
title: dragHandle
description: Options for the drag handles available in column series.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragHandle-className
title: className
description: The class name of the drag handles. Defaults to `highcharts-drag-handle`.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragHandle-color
title: color
description: The fill color of the drag handles.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragHandle-lineColor
title: lineColor
description: The line color of the drag handles.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragHandle-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: The line width for the drag handles.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragHandle-zIndex
title: zIndex
description: The z index for the drag handles.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragMaxX
title: dragMaxX
description: Set the maximum X value the points can be moved to.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragMaxY
title: dragMaxY
description: Set the maximum Y value the points can be moved to.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragMinX
title: dragMinX
description: Set the minimum X value the points can be moved to.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragMinY
title: dragMinY
description: Set the minimum Y value the points can be moved to.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragPrecisionX
title: dragPrecisionX
description:
The X precision value to drag to for this series. Set to 0 to disable. By
default this is disabled, except for category axes, where the default is
`1`.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragPrecisionY
title: dragPrecisionY
description:
The Y precision value to drag to for this series. Set to 0 to disable. By
default this is disabled, except for category axes, where the default is
`1`.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragSensitivity
title: dragSensitivity
description:
The amount of pixels to drag the pointer before it counts as a drag
operation. This prevents drag/drop to fire when just clicking or
selecting points.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-draggableX
title: draggableX
description: Enable dragging in the X dimension.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-draggableY
title: draggableY
description:
Enable dragging in the Y dimension. Note that this is not supported for
TreeGrid axes (the default axis type in Gantt charts).

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-groupBy
title: groupBy
description:
Group the points by a property. Points with the same property value will
be grouped together when moving.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-guideBox
title: guideBox
description:
Style options for the guide box. The guide box has one state by default,
the `default` state.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-guideBox-default
title: default
description: Style options for the guide box default state.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-guideBox-default-className
title: className
description:
CSS class name of the guide box in this state. Defaults to
`highcharts-drag-box-default`.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-guideBox-default-color
title: color
description: Guide box fill color.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-guideBox-default-cursor
title: cursor
description: Guide box cursor.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-guideBox-default-lineColor
title: lineColor
description: Color of the border around the guide box.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-guideBox-default-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: Width of the line around the guide box.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-guideBox-default-zIndex
title: zIndex
description: Guide box zIndex.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-liveRedraw
title: liveRedraw
description:
Update points as they are dragged. If false, a guide box is drawn to
illustrate the new point size.

name: plotOptions-series-enableMouseTracking
title: enableMouseTracking
description:
Enable or disable the mouse tracking for a specific series. This
includes point tooltips and click events on graphs and points. For
large datasets it improves performance.

name: plotOptions-series-events
title: events
description:
General event handlers for the series items. These event hooks can
also be attached to the series at run time using the
`Highcharts.addEvent` function.

name: plotOptions-series-events-afterAnimate
title: afterAnimate
description:
Fires after the series has finished its initial animation, or in case
animation is disabled, immediately as the series is displayed.

name: plotOptions-series-events-checkboxClick
title: checkboxClick
description:
Fires when the checkbox next to the series' name in the legend is
clicked. One parameter, `event`, is passed to the function. The state
of the checkbox is found by `event.checked`. The checked item is
found by `event.item`. Return `false` to prevent the default action
which is to toggle the select state of the series.

name: plotOptions-series-events-click
title: click
description:
Fires when the series is clicked. One parameter, `event`, is passed
to the function, containing common event information. Additionally,
`event.point` holds a pointer to the nearest point on the graph.

name: plotOptions-series-events-hide
title: hide
description:
Fires when the series is hidden after chart generation time, either
by clicking the legend item or by calling `.hide()`.

name: plotOptions-series-events-mouseOut
title: mouseOut
description:
Fires when the mouse leaves the graph. One parameter, `event`, is
passed to the function, containing common event information. If the
[stickyTracking](#plotOptions.series) option is true, `mouseOut`
doesn't happen before the mouse enters another graph or leaves the
plot area.

name: plotOptions-series-events-mouseOver
title: mouseOver
description:
Fires when the mouse enters the graph. One parameter, `event`, is
passed to the function, containing common event information.

name: plotOptions-series-events-show
title: show
description:
Fires when the series is shown after chart generation time, either
by clicking the legend item or by calling `.show()`.

name: plotOptions-series-findNearestPointBy
title: findNearestPointBy
description:
Determines whether the series should look for the nearest point
in both dimensions or just the x-dimension when hovering the series.
Defaults to `'xy'` for scatter series and `'x'` for most other
series. If the data has duplicate x-values, it is recommended to
set this to `'xy'` to allow hovering over all points.

Applies only to series types using nearest neighbor search (not
direct hover) for tooltip.

name: plotOptions-series-gapSize
title: gapSize
description:
Defines when to display a gap in the graph, together with the
[gapUnit](plotOptions.series.gapUnit) option.

In case when `dataGrouping` is enabled, points can be grouped
into a larger time span. This can make the grouped points to
have a greater distance than the absolute value of `gapSize`
property, which will result in disappearing graph completely.
To prevent this situation the mentioned distance between
grouped points is used instead of previously defined
`gapSize`.

In practice, this option is most often used to visualize gaps
in time series. In a stock chart, intraday data is available
for daytime hours, while gaps will appear in nights and
weekends.

name: plotOptions-series-gapUnit
title: gapUnit
description:
Together with [gapSize](plotOptions.series.gapSize), this
option defines where to draw gaps in the graph.

When the `gapUnit` is `"relative"` (default), a gap size of 5
means that if the distance between two points is greater than
5 times that of the two closest points, the graph will be
broken.

When the `gapUnit` is `"value"`, the gap is based on absolute
axis values, which on a datetime axis is milliseconds. This
also applies to the navigator series that inherits gap
options from the base series.

name: plotOptions-series-getExtremesFromAll
title: getExtremesFromAll
description:
Whether to use the Y extremes of the total chart width or only the
zoomed area when zooming in on parts of the X axis. By default, the
Y axis adjusts to the min and max of the visible data. Cartesian
series only.

name: plotOptions-series-inactiveOtherPoints
title: inactiveOtherPoints
description:
Highlight only the hovered point and fade the remaining points.

Scatter-type series require enabling the 'inactive' marker state and
adjusting opacity. Note that this approach could affect performance
with large datasets.

name: plotOptions-series-includeInDataExport
title: includeInDataExport
description:
When set to `false` will prevent the series data from being included in
any form of data export.

Since version 6.0.0 until 7.1.0 the option was existing undocumented
as `includeInCSVExport`.

name: plotOptions-series-keys
title: keys
description:
An array specifying which option maps to which key in the data point
array. This makes it convenient to work with unstructured data arrays
from different sources.

name: plotOptions-series-label
title: label
description:
Series labels are placed as close to the series as possible in a
natural way, seeking to avoid other series. The goal of this
feature is to make the chart more easily readable, like if a
human designer placed the labels in the optimal position.

The series labels currently work with series types having a
`graph` or an `area`.

name: plotOptions-series-label-boxesToAvoid
title: boxesToAvoid
description:
An array of boxes to avoid when laying out the labels. Each
item has a `left`, `right`, `top` and `bottom` property.

name: plotOptions-series-label-connectorAllowed
title: connectorAllowed
description:
Allow labels to be placed distant to the graph if necessary,
and draw a connector line to the graph. Setting this option
to true may decrease the performance significantly, since the
algorithm with systematically search for open spaces in the
whole plot area. Visually, it may also result in a more
cluttered chart, though more of the series will be labeled.

name: plotOptions-series-label-connectorNeighbourDistance
title: connectorNeighbourDistance
description:
If the label is closer than this to a neighbor graph, draw a
connector.

name: plotOptions-series-label-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable the series label per series.

name: plotOptions-series-label-format
title: format
description:
A format string for the label, with support for a subset of
HTML. Variables are enclosed by curly brackets. Available
variables are `name`, `options.xxx`, `color` and other
members from the `series` object. Use this option also to set
a static text for the label.

name: plotOptions-series-label-formatter
title: formatter
description:
Callback function to format each of the series' labels. The
`this` keyword refers to the series object. By default the
`formatter` is undefined and the `series.name` is rendered.
Since v12.6.0, the callback also receives `ctx` as the first argument,
so that arrow functions can access the same context as regular
functions using `this`.

name: plotOptions-series-label-maxFontSize
title: maxFontSize
description:
For area-like series, allow the font size to vary so that
small areas get a smaller font size. The default applies this
effect to area-like series but not line-like series.

name: plotOptions-series-label-minFontSize
title: minFontSize
description:
For area-like series, allow the font size to vary so that
small areas get a smaller font size. The default applies this
effect to area-like series but not line-like series.

name: plotOptions-series-label-onArea
title: onArea
description:
Draw the label on the area of an area series. By default it
is drawn on the area. Set it to `false` to draw it next to
the graph instead.

name: plotOptions-series-label-style
title: style
description:
Styles for the series label. The color defaults to the series
color, or a contrast color if `onArea`.

name: plotOptions-series-label-useHTML
title: useHTML
description: Whether to use HTML to render the series label.

name: plotOptions-series-legendSymbol
title: legendSymbol
description:
What type of legend symbol to render for this series. Can be one of
`areaMarker`, `lineMarker` or `rectangle`.

name: plotOptions-series-legendSymbolColor
title: legendSymbolColor
description:
Defines the color of the legend symbol for this series. Defaults to
undefined, in which case the series color is used. Does not work with
styled mode.

name: plotOptions-series-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: Pixel width of the graph line.

name: plotOptions-series-linecap
title: linecap
description: The line cap used for line ends and line joins on the graph.

name: plotOptions-series-linkedTo
title: linkedTo
description:
The [id](#series.id) of another series to link to. Additionally,
the value can be ":previous" to link to the previous series. When
two series are linked, only the first one appears in the legend.
Toggling the visibility of this also toggles the linked series.

If master series uses data sorting and linked series does not have
its own sorting definition, the linked series will be sorted in the
same order as the master one.

If a `compare` value is not set on a linked series, it will be inherited
from the parent series.

name: plotOptions-series-marker
title: marker
description:
Options for the point markers of line and scatter-like series. Properties
like `fillColor`, `lineColor` and `lineWidth` define the visual
appearance of the markers. The `symbol` option defines the shape. Other
series types, like column series, don't have markers, but have visual
options on the series level instead.

In styled mode, the markers can be styled with the `.highcharts-point`,
`.highcharts-point-hover` and `.highcharts-point-select` class names.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-enabled
title: enabled
description:
Enable or disable the point marker. If `undefined`, the markers
are hidden when the data is dense, and shown for more widespread
data points.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-enabledThreshold
title: enabledThreshold
description:
The threshold for how dense the point markers should be before
they are hidden, given that `enabled` is not defined. The number
indicates the horizontal distance between the two closest points
in the series, as multiples of the `marker.radius`. In other
words, the default value of 2 means points are hidden if
overlapping horizontally.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-fillColor
title: fillColor
description:
The fill color of the point marker. When `undefined`, the series'
or point's color is used.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-height
title: height
description:
Image markers only. Set the image width explicitly. When using
this option, a `width` must also be set.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-lineColor
title: lineColor
description:
The color of the point marker's outline. When `undefined`, the
series' or point's color is used.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: The width of the point marker's outline.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-radius
title: radius
description: The radius of the point marker.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-states
title: states
description: States for a single point marker.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-states-hover
title: hover
description: The hover state for a single point marker.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-states-hover-animation
title: animation
description: Animation when hovering over the marker.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-states-hover-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable or disable the point marker.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-states-hover-fillColor
title: fillColor
description:
The fill color of the marker in hover state. When
`undefined`, the series' or point's fillColor for normal
state is used.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-states-hover-lineColor
title: lineColor
description:
The color of the point marker's outline. When
`undefined`, the series' or point's lineColor for normal
state is used.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-states-hover-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description:
The width of the point marker's outline. When
`undefined`, the series' or point's lineWidth for normal
state is used.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-states-hover-lineWidthPlus
title: lineWidthPlus
description: The additional line width for a hovered point.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-states-hover-radius
title: radius
description:
The radius of the point marker. In hover state, it
defaults to the normal state's radius + 2 as per the
[radiusPlus](#plotOptions.series.marker.states.hover.radiusPlus)
option.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-states-hover-radiusPlus
title: radiusPlus
description:
The number of pixels to increase the radius of the
hovered point.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-states-normal
title: normal
description:
The normal state of a single point marker. Currently only
used for setting animation when returning to normal state
from hover.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-states-normal-animation
title: animation
description: Animation when returning to normal state after hovering.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-states-select
title: select
description:
The appearance of the point marker when selected. In order to
allow a point to be selected, set the
`series.allowPointSelect` option to true.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-states-select-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable or disable visible feedback for selection.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-states-select-fillColor
title: fillColor
description: The fill color of the point marker.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-states-select-lineColor
title: lineColor
description:
The color of the point marker's outline. When
`undefined`, the series' or point's color is used.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-states-select-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: The width of the point marker's outline.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-states-select-radius
title: radius
description:
The radius of the point marker. In hover state, it
defaults to the normal state's radius + 2.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-symbol
title: symbol
description:
A predefined shape or symbol for the marker. When undefined, the
symbol is pulled from options.symbols. Other possible values are
`'circle'`, `'square'`,`'diamond'`, `'triangle'` and
`'triangle-down'`.

Additionally, the URL to a graphic can be given on this form:
`'url(graphic.png)'`. Note that for the image to be applied to
exported charts, its URL needs to be accessible by the export
server.

Custom callbacks for symbol path generation can also be added to
`Highcharts.SVGRenderer.prototype.symbols`. The callback is then
used by its method name, as shown in the demo.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-width
title: width
description:
Image markers only. Set the image width explicitly. When using
this option, a `height` must also be set.

name: plotOptions-series-negativeColor
title: negativeColor
description:
The color for the parts of the graph or points that are below the
[threshold](#plotOptions.series.threshold). Note that `zones` takes
precedence over the negative color. Using `negativeColor` is
equivalent to applying a zone with value of 0.

name: plotOptions-series-nullInteraction
title: nullInteraction
description:
Whether or not data-points with the value of `null` should be interactive.
When this is set to `true`, tooltips may highlight these points, and this
option also enables keyboard navigation for such points. Format options
for such points include [`nullFormat`](#tooltip.nullFormat) and
[`nullFormatter`](#tooltip.nullFormatter). Works for these series:
`line`, `spline`, `area`, `area-spline`, `column`, `bar`, and
`timeline`.

name: plotOptions-series-onPoint
title: onPoint
description:
Options for the _Series on point_ feature. Only `pie` and `sunburst` series
are supported at this moment.

name: plotOptions-series-onPoint-connectorOptions
title: connectorOptions
description:
Options for the connector in the _Series on point_ feature.

In styled mode, the connector can be styled with the
`.highcharts-connector-seriesonpoint` class name.

name: plotOptions-series-onPoint-connectorOptions-dashstyle
title: dashstyle
description: A name for the dash style to use for the connector.

name: plotOptions-series-onPoint-connectorOptions-stroke
title: stroke
description: Color of the connector line. By default it's the series' color.

name: plotOptions-series-onPoint-connectorOptions-width
title: width
description: Pixel width of the connector line.

name: plotOptions-series-onPoint-id
title: id
description:
The `id` of the point that we connect the series to. Only points with a given
`plotX` and `plotY` values and map points are valid.

name: plotOptions-series-onPoint-position
title: position
description:
Options allowing to set a position and an offset of the series in the
_Series on point_ feature.

name: plotOptions-series-onPoint-position-offsetX
title: offsetX
description:
Series center offset from the original x position. If defined, the connector
line is drawn connecting original position with new position.

name: plotOptions-series-onPoint-position-offsetY
title: offsetY
description:
Series center offset from the original y position. If defined, the connector
line is drawn from original position to a new position.

name: plotOptions-series-onPoint-position-x
title: x
description:
X position of the series center. By default, the series is displayed on the
point that it is connected to.

name: plotOptions-series-onPoint-position-y
title: y
description:
Y position of the series center. By default, the series is displayed on the
point that it is connected to.

name: plotOptions-series-opacity
title: opacity
description: Opacity of a series parts: line, fill (e.g. area) and dataLabels.

name: plotOptions-series-point
title: point
description: Properties for each single point.

name: plotOptions-series-point-events
title: events
description: Events for each single point.

name: plotOptions-series-point-events-click
title: click
description:
Fires when a point is clicked. One parameter, `event`, is passed
to the function, containing common event information.

If the `series.allowPointSelect` option is true, the default
action for the point's click event is to toggle the point's
select state. Returning `false` cancels this action.

name: plotOptions-series-point-events-drag
title: drag
description:
Callback that fires while dragging a point. The mouse event is passed in
as parameter. The original data can be accessed from `e.origin`, and the
new point values can be accessed from `e.newPoints`. If there is only a
single point being updated, it can be accessed from `e.newPoint` for
simplicity, and its ID can be accessed from `e.newPointId`. The `this`
context is the point being dragged. To stop the default drag action,
return false. See [drag and drop options](plotOptions.series.dragDrop).

name: plotOptions-series-point-events-dragStart
title: dragStart
description:
Callback that fires when starting to drag a point. The mouse event object
is passed in as an argument. If a drag handle is used, `e.updateProp` is
set to the data property being dragged. The `this` context is the point.
See [drag and drop options](plotOptions.series.dragDrop).

name: plotOptions-series-point-events-drop
title: drop
description:
Callback that fires when the point is dropped. The parameters passed are
the same as for [drag](#plotOptions.series.point.events.drag). To stop
the default drop action, return false. See
[drag and drop options](plotOptions.series.dragDrop).

name: plotOptions-series-point-events-mouseOut
title: mouseOut
description:
Fires when the mouse leaves the area close to the point. One
parameter, `event`, is passed to the function, containing common
event information.

name: plotOptions-series-point-events-mouseOver
title: mouseOver
description:
Fires when the mouse enters the area close to the point. One
parameter, `event`, is passed to the function, containing common
event information.

Returning `false` cancels the default behavior, which is to show a
tooltip for the point.

name: plotOptions-series-point-events-remove
title: remove
description:
Fires when the point is removed using the `.remove()` method. One
parameter, `event`, is passed to the function. Returning `false`
cancels the operation.

name: plotOptions-series-point-events-select
title: select
description:
Fires when the point is selected either programmatically or
following a click on the point. One parameter, `event`, is passed
to the function. Returning `false` cancels the operation.

name: plotOptions-series-point-events-unselect
title: unselect
description:
Fires when the point is unselected either programmatically or
following a click on the point. One parameter, `event`, is passed
to the function.
 Returning `false` cancels the operation.

name: plotOptions-series-point-events-update
title: update
description:
Fires when the point is updated programmatically through the
`.update()` method. One parameter, `event`, is passed to the
function. The new point options can be accessed through
`event.options`. Returning `false` cancels the operation.

name: plotOptions-series-pointInterval
title: pointInterval
description:
If no x values are given for the points in a series, `pointInterval`
defines the interval of the x values. For example, if a series
contains one value every decade starting from year 0, set
`pointInterval` to `10`. In true `datetime` axes, the `pointInterval`
is set in milliseconds.

It can be also be combined with `pointIntervalUnit` to draw irregular
time intervals.

If combined with `relativeXValue`, an x value can be set on each
point, and the `pointInterval` is added x times to the `pointStart`
setting.

Please note that this options applies to the _series data_, not the
interval of the axis ticks, which is independent.

name: plotOptions-series-pointIntervalUnit
title: pointIntervalUnit
description:
On datetime series, this allows for setting the
[pointInterval](#plotOptions.series.pointInterval) to irregular time
units, `day`, `month` and `year`. A day is usually the same as 24
hours, but `pointIntervalUnit` also takes the DST crossover into
consideration when dealing with local time. Combine this option with
`pointInterval` to draw weeks, quarters, 6 months, 10 years etc.

Please note that this options applies to the _series data_, not the
interval of the axis ticks, which is independent.

name: plotOptions-series-pointPlacement
title: pointPlacement
description:
Possible values: `"on"`, `"between"`, `number`.

In a column chart, when pointPlacement is `"on"`, the point will not
create any padding of the X axis. In a polar column chart this means
that the first column points directly north. If the pointPlacement is
`"between"`, the columns will be laid out between ticks. This is
useful for example for visualizing an amount between two points in
time or in a certain sector of a polar chart.

Since Highcharts 3.0.2, the point placement can also be numeric,
where 0 is on the axis value, -0.5 is between this value and the
previous, and 0.5 is between this value and the next. Unlike the
textual options, numeric point placement options won't affect axis
padding.

Note that pointPlacement needs a [pointRange](#plotOptions.series.pointRange) to work. For column series this is
computed, but for line-type series it needs to be set.

For the `xrange` series type and gantt charts, if the Y axis is a
category axis, the `pointPlacement` applies to the Y axis rather than
the (typically datetime) X axis.

Defaults to `undefined` in cartesian charts, `"between"` in polar
charts.

name: plotOptions-series-pointStart
title: pointStart
description:
If no x values are given for the points in a series, `pointStart`
defines on what value to start. For example, if a series contains one
yearly value starting from 1945, set `pointStart` to 1945.

The `pointStart` setting can be a number, or a datetime string that is
parsed according to the `time.timezone` setting.

If combined with `relativeXValue`, an x value can be set on each
point. The x value from the point options is multiplied by
`pointInterval` and added to `pointStart` to produce a modified x
value.

name: plotOptions-series-relativeXValue
title: relativeXValue
description:
When true, X values in the data set are relative to the current
`pointStart`, `pointInterval` and `pointIntervalUnit` settings. This
allows compression of the data for datasets with irregular X values.

The real X values are computed on the formula `f(x) = ax + b`, where
`a` is the `pointInterval` (optionally with a time unit given by
`pointIntervalUnit`), and `b` is the `pointStart`.

name: plotOptions-series-selected
title: selected
description:
Whether to select the series initially. If `showCheckbox` is true,
the checkbox next to the series name in the legend will be checked
for a selected series.

name: plotOptions-series-shadow
title: shadow
description:
Whether to apply a drop shadow to the graph line. Since 2.3 the
shadow can be an object configuration containing `color`, `offsetX`,
`offsetY`, `opacity` and `width`.

Note that in some cases, like stacked columns or other dense layouts, the
series may cast shadows on each other. In that case, the
`chart.seriesGroupShadow` allows applying a common drop shadow to the
whole series group.

name: plotOptions-series-showCheckbox
title: showCheckbox
description:
If true, a checkbox is displayed next to the legend item to allow
selecting the series. The state of the checkbox is determined by
the `selected` option.

name: plotOptions-series-showInLegend
title: showInLegend
description:
Whether to display this particular series or series type in the
legend. Standalone series are shown in legend by default, and linked
series are not. Since v7.2.0 it is possible to show series that use
colorAxis by setting this option to `true`.

name: plotOptions-series-softThreshold
title: softThreshold
description:
When this is true, the series will not cause the Y axis to cross
the zero plane (or [threshold](#plotOptions.series.threshold) option)
unless the data actually crosses the plane.

For example, if `softThreshold` is `false`, a series of 0, 1, 2,
3 will make the Y axis show negative values according to the
`minPadding` option. If `softThreshold` is `true`, the Y axis starts
at 0.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification
title: sonification
description: Sonification/audio chart options for a series.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks
title: contextTracks
description:
Context tracks for this series. Context tracks are tracks that are not
tied to data points.

Given as an array of instrument tracks, speech tracks, or a mix of both.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-activeWhen
title: activeWhen
description:
Define a condition for when a track should be active and not.

Can either be a function callback or a configuration object.

If a function is used, it should return a `boolean` for whether
or not the track should be active. The function is called for
each audio event, and receives a parameter object with `time`,
and potentially `point` and `value` properties depending on the
track. `point` is available if the audio event is related to a
data point. `value` is available if the track is used as a
context track, and `valueInterval` is used.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-activeWhen-crossingDown
title: crossingDown
description:
Track is only active when `prop` was above, and is now at or
below this value.

If both `crossingUp` and `crossingDown` are defined, the track
is active if either condition is met.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-activeWhen-crossingUp
title: crossingUp
description:
Track is only active when `prop` was below, and is now at or
above this value.

If both `crossingUp` and `crossingDown` are defined, the track
is active if either condition is met.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-activeWhen-max
title: max
description: Track is only active when `prop` is below or at this value.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-activeWhen-min
title: min
description: Track is only active when `prop` is above or at this value.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-activeWhen-prop
title: prop
description: The point property to compare, for example `y` or `x`.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-instrument
title: instrument
description:
Instrument to use for playing.

Can either be a string referencing a synth preset, or it can be
a synth configuration object.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-frequency
title: frequency
description: Frequency in Hertz of notes. Overrides pitch mapping if set.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-gapBetweenNotes
title: gapBetweenNotes
description:
Gap in milliseconds between notes if pitch is mapped to an
array of notes.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-highpass
title: highpass
description:
Mapping options for the highpass filter.

A highpass filter lets high frequencies through, but stops
low frequencies, making the sound thinner.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-highpass-frequency
title: frequency
description: Map to filter frequency in Hertz from 1 to 20,000Hz.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-highpass-resonance
title: resonance
description:
Map to filter resonance in dB. Can be negative to cause a
dip, or positive to cause a bump.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-lowpass
title: lowpass
description:
Mapping options for the lowpass filter.

A lowpass filter lets low frequencies through, but stops high
frequencies, making the sound more dull.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-lowpass-frequency
title: frequency
description: Map to filter frequency in Hertz from 1 to 20,000Hz.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-lowpass-resonance
title: resonance
description:
Map to filter resonance in dB. Can be negative to cause a
dip, or positive to cause a bump.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-noteDuration
title: noteDuration
description:
Note duration determines for how long a note plays, in
milliseconds.

It only affects instruments that are able to play
continuous sustained notes. Examples of these instruments
from the presets include `flute`, `saxophone`, `trumpet`,
`sawsynth`, `wobble`, `basic1`, `basic2`, `sine`,
`sineGlide`, `triangle`, `square`, `sawtooth`, `noise`,
`filteredNoise`, and `wind`.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-pan
title: pan
description:
Pan refers to the stereo panning position of the sound.
It is defined from -1 (left) to 1 (right).

By default it is mapped to `x`, making the sound move from
left to right as the chart plays.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-pitch
title: pitch
description:
Musical pitch refers to how high or low notes are played.

By default it is mapped to `y` so low `y` values are played
with a lower pitch, and high values are played with a higher
pitch.

Pitch mapping has a few extra features compared to other
audio parameters.

Firstly, it accepts not only number values, but also string
values denoting note names. These are given in the form
`<note><octave>`, for example `"c6"` or `"F#2"`.

Secondly, it is possible to map pitch to an array of notes.
In this case, the `[gapBetweenNotes](#sonification.defaultInstrumentOptions.mapping.gapBetweenNotes)`
mapping determines the delay between these notes.

Thirdly, it is possible to define a musical scale to follow
when mapping.

Can be set to a fixed value, an array, a prop to map to, a
function, or a mapping object.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-pitch-scale
title: scale
description:
Map pitches to a musical scale. The scale is defined as an
array of semitone offsets from the root note.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-playDelay
title: playDelay
description:
Milliseconds to wait before playing, comes in addition to
the time determined by the `time` mapping.

Can also be negative to play before the mapped time.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-time
title: time
description:
Time mapping determines what time each point plays. It is
defined as an offset in milliseconds, where 0 means it
plays immediately when the chart is sonified.

By default time is mapped to `x`, meaning points with the
lowest `x` value plays first, and points with the highest
`x` value plays last.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-time-mapFunction
title: mapFunction
description: How to perform the mapping.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-time-mapTo
title: mapTo
description:
A point property to map the mapping parameter to.

A negative sign `-` can be placed before the property name
to make mapping inverted.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-time-max
title: max
description:
The maximum value for the audio parameter. This is the
highest value the audio parameter will be mapped to.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-time-min
title: min
description:
The minimum value for the audio parameter. This is the
lowest value the audio parameter will be mapped to.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-time-value
title: value
description:
A fixed value to use for the prop when mapping.

For example, if mapping to `y`, setting value to `4` will
map as if all points had a y value of 4.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-time-within
title: within
description:
What data values to map the parameter within.

Mapping within `"series"` will make the lowest value point
in the series map to the min audio parameter value, and the
highest value will map to the max audio parameter.

Mapping within `"chart"` will make the lowest value point in
the whole chart map to the min audio parameter value, and
the highest value in the whole chart will map to the max
audio parameter.

You can also map within the X or Y axis of each series.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-tremolo
title: tremolo
description:
Mapping options for tremolo effects.

Tremolo is repeated changes of volume over time.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-tremolo-depth
title: depth
description:
Map to tremolo depth, from 0 to 1.

This determines the intensity of the tremolo effect, how
much the volume changes.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-tremolo-speed
title: speed
description:
Map to tremolo speed, from 0 to 1.

This determines the speed of the tremolo effect, how fast
the volume changes.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-volume
title: volume
description: The volume of notes, from 0 to 1.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-rate
title: rate
description: Rate mapping for speech tracks.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-rate-mapFunction
title: mapFunction
description: How to perform the mapping.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-rate-mapTo
title: mapTo
description:
A point property to map the mapping parameter to.

A negative sign `-` can be placed before the property name
to make mapping inverted.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-rate-max
title: max
description:
The maximum value for the audio parameter. This is the
highest value the audio parameter will be mapped to.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-rate-min
title: min
description:
The minimum value for the audio parameter. This is the
lowest value the audio parameter will be mapped to.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-rate-value
title: value
description:
A fixed value to use for the prop when mapping.

For example, if mapping to `y`, setting value to `4` will
map as if all points had a y value of 4.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-rate-within
title: within
description:
What data values to map the parameter within.

Mapping within `"series"` will make the lowest value point
in the series map to the min audio parameter value, and the
highest value will map to the max audio parameter.

Mapping within `"chart"` will make the lowest value point in
the whole chart map to the min audio parameter value, and
the highest value in the whole chart will map to the max
audio parameter.

You can also map within the X or Y axis of each series.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-text
title: text
description: Text mapping for speech tracks.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-midiName
title: midiName
description:
Name to use for a track when exporting to MIDI.
By default it uses the series name if the track is related to
a series.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-pointGrouping
title: pointGrouping
description: Options for point grouping, specifically for instrument tracks.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-pointGrouping-algorithm
title: algorithm
description:
The grouping algorithm, deciding which points to keep when
grouping a set of points together. By default `"minmax"` is
used, which keeps both the minimum and maximum points.

The other algorithms will either keep the first point in the
group (time wise), last point, middle point, or both the first
and the last point.

The timing of the resulting point(s) is then adjusted to play
evenly, regardless of its original position within the group.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-pointGrouping-enabled
title: enabled
description: Whether or not to group points

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-pointGrouping-groupTimespan
title: groupTimespan
description:
The size of each group in milliseconds. Audio events closer than
this are grouped together.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-pointGrouping-prop
title: prop
description:
The data property for each point to compare when deciding which
points to keep in the group.

By default it is "y", which means that if the `"minmax"`
algorithm is used, the two points the group with the lowest and
highest `y` value will be kept, and the others not played.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-roundToMusicalNotes
title: roundToMusicalNotes
description:
Round pitch mapping to musical notes.

If `false`, will play the exact mapped note, even if it is out
of tune compared to the musical notes as defined by 440Hz
standard tuning.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-showPlayMarker
title: showPlayMarker
description: Show play marker (tooltip and/or crosshair) for a track.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-type
title: type
description:
Type of track. Always `"instrument"` for instrument tracks, and
`"speech"` for speech tracks.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-timeInterval
title: timeInterval
description:
Set a context track to play periodically every `timeInterval`
milliseconds while the sonification is playing.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-valueInterval
title: valueInterval
description:
Set a context track to play periodically every `valueInterval`
units of a data property `valueProp` while the sonification is
playing.

For example, setting `valueProp` to `x` and `valueInterval` to 5
will play the context track for every 5th X value.

The context audio events will be mapped to time according to the
prop value relative to the min/max values for that prop.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-valueMapFunction
title: valueMapFunction
description:
How to map context events to time when using the `valueInterval`
option.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-valueProp
title: valueProp
description: The point property to play context for when using `valueInterval`.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions
title: defaultInstrumentOptions
description: Default options for all this series' instrument tracks.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-activeWhen
title: activeWhen
description:
Define a condition for when a track should be active and not.

Can either be a function callback or a configuration object.

If a function is used, it should return a `boolean` for whether
or not the track should be active. The function is called for
each audio event, and receives a parameter object with `time`,
and potentially `point` and `value` properties depending on the
track. `point` is available if the audio event is related to a
data point. `value` is available if the track is used as a
context track, and `valueInterval` is used.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-activeWhen-crossingDown
title: crossingDown
description:
Track is only active when `prop` was above, and is now at or
below this value.

If both `crossingUp` and `crossingDown` are defined, the track
is active if either condition is met.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-activeWhen-crossingUp
title: crossingUp
description:
Track is only active when `prop` was below, and is now at or
above this value.

If both `crossingUp` and `crossingDown` are defined, the track
is active if either condition is met.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-activeWhen-max
title: max
description: Track is only active when `prop` is below or at this value.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-activeWhen-min
title: min
description: Track is only active when `prop` is above or at this value.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-activeWhen-prop
title: prop
description: The point property to compare, for example `y` or `x`.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-instrument
title: instrument
description:
Instrument to use for playing.

Can either be a string referencing a synth preset, or it can be
a synth configuration object.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping
title: mapping
description:
Mapping options for the audio parameters.

All parameters can be either:
 - A string, referencing a point property to map to.
 - A number, setting the value of the audio parameter directly.
 - A callback function, returning the value programmatically.
 - An object defining detailed configuration of the mapping.

If a function is used, it should return the desired value for
the audio parameter. The function is called for each audio event
to be played, and receives a context object parameter with
`time`, and potentially `point` and `value` depending on the
track. `point` is available if the audio event is related to a
data point, and `value` is available if the track is used for a
context track using `valueInterval`.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-frequency
title: frequency
description: Frequency in Hertz of notes. Overrides pitch mapping if set.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-gapBetweenNotes
title: gapBetweenNotes
description:
Gap in milliseconds between notes if pitch is mapped to an
array of notes.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-highpass
title: highpass
description:
Mapping options for the highpass filter.

A highpass filter lets high frequencies through, but stops
low frequencies, making the sound thinner.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-highpass-frequency
title: frequency
description: Map to filter frequency in Hertz from 1 to 20,000Hz.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-highpass-resonance
title: resonance
description:
Map to filter resonance in dB. Can be negative to cause a
dip, or positive to cause a bump.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-lowpass
title: lowpass
description:
Mapping options for the lowpass filter.

A lowpass filter lets low frequencies through, but stops high
frequencies, making the sound more dull.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-lowpass-frequency
title: frequency
description: Map to filter frequency in Hertz from 1 to 20,000Hz.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-lowpass-resonance
title: resonance
description:
Map to filter resonance in dB. Can be negative to cause a
dip, or positive to cause a bump.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-noteDuration
title: noteDuration
description:
Note duration determines for how long a note plays, in
milliseconds.

It only affects instruments that are able to play
continuous sustained notes. Examples of these instruments
from the presets include `flute`, `saxophone`, `trumpet`,
`sawsynth`, `wobble`, `basic1`, `basic2`, `sine`,
`sineGlide`, `triangle`, `square`, `sawtooth`, `noise`,
`filteredNoise`, and `wind`.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-pan
title: pan
description:
Pan refers to the stereo panning position of the sound.
It is defined from -1 (left) to 1 (right).

By default it is mapped to `x`, making the sound move from
left to right as the chart plays.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-pitch
title: pitch
description:
Musical pitch refers to how high or low notes are played.

By default it is mapped to `y` so low `y` values are played
with a lower pitch, and high values are played with a higher
pitch.

Pitch mapping has a few extra features compared to other
audio parameters.

Firstly, it accepts not only number values, but also string
values denoting note names. These are given in the form
`<note><octave>`, for example `"c6"` or `"F#2"`.

Secondly, it is possible to map pitch to an array of notes.
In this case, the `[gapBetweenNotes](#sonification.defaultInstrumentOptions.mapping.gapBetweenNotes)`
mapping determines the delay between these notes.

Thirdly, it is possible to define a musical scale to follow
when mapping.

Can be set to a fixed value, an array, a prop to map to, a
function, or a mapping object.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-pitch-scale
title: scale
description:
Map pitches to a musical scale. The scale is defined as an
array of semitone offsets from the root note.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-playDelay
title: playDelay
description:
Milliseconds to wait before playing, comes in addition to
the time determined by the `time` mapping.

Can also be negative to play before the mapped time.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-time
title: time
description:
Time mapping determines what time each point plays. It is
defined as an offset in milliseconds, where 0 means it
plays immediately when the chart is sonified.

By default time is mapped to `x`, meaning points with the
lowest `x` value plays first, and points with the highest
`x` value plays last.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-time-mapFunction
title: mapFunction
description: How to perform the mapping.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-time-mapTo
title: mapTo
description:
A point property to map the mapping parameter to.

A negative sign `-` can be placed before the property name
to make mapping inverted.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-time-max
title: max
description:
The maximum value for the audio parameter. This is the
highest value the audio parameter will be mapped to.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-time-min
title: min
description:
The minimum value for the audio parameter. This is the
lowest value the audio parameter will be mapped to.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-time-value
title: value
description:
A fixed value to use for the prop when mapping.

For example, if mapping to `y`, setting value to `4` will
map as if all points had a y value of 4.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-time-within
title: within
description:
What data values to map the parameter within.

Mapping within `"series"` will make the lowest value point
in the series map to the min audio parameter value, and the
highest value will map to the max audio parameter.

Mapping within `"chart"` will make the lowest value point in
the whole chart map to the min audio parameter value, and
the highest value in the whole chart will map to the max
audio parameter.

You can also map within the X or Y axis of each series.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-tremolo
title: tremolo
description:
Mapping options for tremolo effects.

Tremolo is repeated changes of volume over time.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-tremolo-depth
title: depth
description:
Map to tremolo depth, from 0 to 1.

This determines the intensity of the tremolo effect, how
much the volume changes.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-tremolo-speed
title: speed
description:
Map to tremolo speed, from 0 to 1.

This determines the speed of the tremolo effect, how fast
the volume changes.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-volume
title: volume
description: The volume of notes, from 0 to 1.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-midiName
title: midiName
description:
Name to use for a track when exporting to MIDI.
By default it uses the series name if the track is related to
a series.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-pointGrouping
title: pointGrouping
description: Options for point grouping, specifically for instrument tracks.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-pointGrouping-algorithm
title: algorithm
description:
The grouping algorithm, deciding which points to keep when
grouping a set of points together. By default `"minmax"` is
used, which keeps both the minimum and maximum points.

The other algorithms will either keep the first point in the
group (time wise), last point, middle point, or both the first
and the last point.

The timing of the resulting point(s) is then adjusted to play
evenly, regardless of its original position within the group.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-pointGrouping-enabled
title: enabled
description: Whether or not to group points

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-pointGrouping-groupTimespan
title: groupTimespan
description:
The size of each group in milliseconds. Audio events closer than
this are grouped together.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-pointGrouping-prop
title: prop
description:
The data property for each point to compare when deciding which
points to keep in the group.

By default it is "y", which means that if the `"minmax"`
algorithm is used, the two points the group with the lowest and
highest `y` value will be kept, and the others not played.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-roundToMusicalNotes
title: roundToMusicalNotes
description:
Round pitch mapping to musical notes.

If `false`, will play the exact mapped note, even if it is out
of tune compared to the musical notes as defined by 440Hz
standard tuning.

Define a condition for when a track should be active and not.

Can either be a function callback or a configuration object.

If a function is used, it should return a `boolean` for whether
or not the track should be active. The function is called for
each audio event, and receives a parameter object with `time`,
and potentially `point` and `value` properties depending on the
track. `point` is available if the audio event is related to a
data point. `value` is available if the track is used as a
context track, and `valueInterval` is used.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-tracks-activeWhen-crossingDown
title: crossingDown
description:
Track is only active when `prop` was above, and is now at or
below this value.

If both `crossingUp` and `crossingDown` are defined, the track
is active if either condition is met.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-tracks-activeWhen-crossingUp
title: crossingUp
description:
Track is only active when `prop` was below, and is now at or
above this value.

If both `crossingUp` and `crossingDown` are defined, the track
is active if either condition is met.
