this are grouped together.

name: series-sonification-tracks-pointGrouping-prop
title: prop
description:
The data property for each point to compare when deciding which
points to keep in the group.

By default it is "y", which means that if the `"minmax"`
algorithm is used, the two points the group with the lowest and
highest `y` value will be kept, and the others not played.

name: series-sonification-tracks-roundToMusicalNotes
title: roundToMusicalNotes
description:
Round pitch mapping to musical notes.

If `false`, will play the exact mapped note, even if it is out
of tune compared to the musical notes as defined by 440Hz
standard tuning.

name: series-sonification-tracks-showPlayMarker
title: showPlayMarker
description: Show play marker (tooltip and/or crosshair) for a track.

name: series-sonification-tracks-type
title: type
description:
Type of track. Always `"instrument"` for instrument tracks, and
`"speech"` for speech tracks.

name: series-stacking
title: stacking
description:
Whether to stack the values of each series on top of each other.
Possible values are null to disable, `"normal"` to stack by
value or `"percent"`.

When stacking is enabled, data must be sorted
in ascending X order.

Some stacking options are related to specific series types. In the
streamgraph series type, the stacking option is set to `"stream"`.
The second one is `"overlap"`, which only applies to waterfall
series.

name: series-states
title: states
description:
A collection of options for different series states.

In addition to the options documented under each state, any option from
the parent series type can be set, with exception of `data` and `states`.

name: series-states-hover
title: hover
description:
Options for the hovered series. These settings override the
normal state options when a series is moused over or touched.

name: series-states-hover-animation
title: animation
description: Animation setting for hovering the graph in line-type series.

name: series-states-hover-animation-duration
title: duration
description:
The duration of the hover animation in milliseconds. By
default the hover state animates quickly in, and slowly
back to normal.

name: series-states-hover-enabled
title: enabled
description:
Enable separate styles for the hovered series to visualize
that the user hovers either the series itself or the legend.

name: series-states-hover-halo
title: halo
description:
Options for the halo appearing around the hovered point in
line-type series as well as outside the hovered slice in pie
charts. By default the halo is filled by the current point or
series color with an opacity of 0.25\. The halo can be
disabled by setting the `halo` option to `null`.

In styled mode, the halo is styled with the
`.highcharts-halo` class, with colors inherited from
`.highcharts-color-{n}`.

name: series-states-hover-halo-attributes
title: attributes
description:
A collection of SVG attributes to override the appearance
of the halo, for example `fill`, `stroke` and
`stroke-width`.

name: series-states-hover-halo-opacity
title: opacity
description:
Opacity for the halo unless a specific fill is overridden
using the `attributes` setting.

name: series-states-hover-halo-size
title: size
description:
The pixel size of the halo. For point markers this is the
radius of the halo. For pie slices it is the width of the
halo outside the slice. For bubbles it defaults to 5 and
is the width of the halo outside the bubble.

name: series-states-hover-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description:
Pixel width of the graph line. By default this property is
undefined, and the `lineWidthPlus` property dictates how much
to increase the linewidth from normal state.

name: series-states-hover-lineWidthPlus
title: lineWidthPlus
description: The additional line width for the graph of a hovered series.

name: series-states-hover-marker
title: marker
description:
In Highcharts 1.0, the appearance of all markers belonging
to the hovered series. For settings on the hover state of the
individual point, see
[marker.states.hover](#plotOptions.series.marker.states.hover).

name: series-states-inactive
title: inactive
description: The opposite state of a hover for series.

name: series-states-inactive-animation
title: animation
description: Animation when not hovering over the marker.

name: series-states-inactive-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable or disable the inactive state for a series

name: series-states-inactive-opacity
title: opacity
description: Opacity of series elements (dataLabels, line, area).

name: series-states-normal
title: normal
description:
The normal state of a series, or for point items in column, pie
and similar series. Currently only used for setting animation
when returning to normal state from hover.

name: series-states-normal-animation
title: animation
description: Animation when returning to normal state after hovering.

name: series-states-select
title: select
description:
Specific options for point in selected states, after being
selected by
[allowPointSelect](#plotOptions.series.allowPointSelect)
or programmatically.

name: series-step
title: step
description:
Whether to apply steps to the line. Possible values are `left`,
`center` and `right`.

name: series-stickyTracking
title: stickyTracking
description:
Sticky tracking of mouse events. When true, the `mouseOut` event on a
series isn't triggered until the mouse moves over another series, or
out of the plot area. When false, the `mouseOut` event on a series is
triggered when the mouse leaves the area around the series' graph or
markers. This also implies the tooltip when not shared. When
`stickyTracking` is false and `tooltip.shared` is false, the tooltip
will be hidden when moving the mouse between series. Defaults to true
for line and area type series, but to false for columns, pies etc.

**Note:** The boost module will force this option because of
technical limitations.

name: series-threshold
title: threshold
description:
The threshold, also called zero level or base level. For line type
series this is only used in conjunction with
[negativeColor](#plotOptions.series.negativeColor).

name: series-tooltip
title: tooltip
description:
A configuration object for the tooltip rendering of each single
series. Properties are inherited from [tooltip](#tooltip), but only
the following properties can be defined on a series level.

name: series-tooltip-clusterFormat
title: clusterFormat
description:
The HTML of the cluster point's in the tooltip. Works only with
marker-clusters module and analogously to
[pointFormat](#tooltip.pointFormat).

The cluster tooltip can be also formatted using
`tooltip.formatter` callback function and `point.isCluster` flag.

name: series-tooltip-dateTimeLabelFormats
title: dateTimeLabelFormats
description:
For series on datetime axes, the date format in the tooltip's
header will by default be guessed based on the closest data points.
This member gives the default string representations used for
each unit. For an overview of the string or object configuration, see
[dateFormat](/class-reference/Highcharts.Time#dateFormat).

name: series-tooltip-distance
title: distance
description: Distance from point to tooltip in pixels.

name: series-tooltip-followPointer
title: followPointer
description:
Whether the tooltip should follow the mouse as it moves across
columns, pie slices and other point types with an extent.
By default it behaves this way for pie, polygon, map, sankey
and wordcloud series by override in the `plotOptions`
for those series types.

Does not apply if [split](#tooltip.split) is `true`.

For touch moves to behave the same way, [followTouchMove](#tooltip.followTouchMove) must be `true` also.

name: series-tooltip-followTouchMove
title: followTouchMove
description:
Whether the tooltip should update as the finger moves on a touch
device. If this is `true` and [chart.panning](#chart.panning) is
set,`followTouchMove` will take over one-finger touches, so the user
needs to use two fingers for zooming and panning.

Note the difference to [followPointer](#tooltip.followPointer) that
only defines the _position_ of the tooltip. If `followPointer` is
false in for example a column series, the tooltip will show above or
below the column, but as `followTouchMove` is true, the tooltip will
jump from column to column as the user swipes across the plot area.

name: series-tooltip-footerFormat
title: footerFormat
description: A string to append to the tooltip format.

name: series-tooltip-format
title: format
description:
A [format string](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting)
for the whole shared tooltip. When format strings are a requirement,
it is usually more convenient to use `headerFormat`, `pointFormat`
and `footerFormat`, but the `format` option allows combining them
into one setting.

The context of the format string is the same as that of the
`tooltip.formatter` callback.

name: series-tooltip-header
title: header
description:
Options for the tooltip header when [tooltip.split](#tooltip.split)
is enabled. The header is the box containing the X value in a split
tooltip.

name: series-tooltip-header-backgroundColor
title: backgroundColor
description:
Background color for the tooltip header when
[tooltip.split](#tooltip.split) is enabled.

name: series-tooltip-header-borderColor
title: borderColor
description:
Border color for the tooltip header when
[tooltip.split](#tooltip.split) is enabled.

name: series-tooltip-header-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description:
The width of the border for the tooltip header when
[tooltip.split](#tooltip.split) is enabled.

name: series-tooltip-header-distance
title: distance
description:
Distance between the plot area and the header (except the
chevron) in a split tooltip, in pixels. The default value makes
the header text align with the axis labels.

name: series-tooltip-header-shape
title: shape
description:
The name of a symbol to use for the border around the tooltip
header. Applies only when [tooltip.split](#tooltip.split) is
enabled.

Custom callbacks for symbol path generation can also be added to
`Highcharts.SVGRenderer.prototype.symbols` the same way as for
[series.marker.symbol](plotOptions.line.marker.symbol).

name: series-tooltip-header-style
title: style
description:
CSS styles for the tooltip header. The default is `{ fontSize:
'1em' }`, ensuring that the header text is the same size as the
axis labels.

name: series-tooltip-headerFormat
title: headerFormat
description:
The HTML of the tooltip header line. The context is the
[Point class](https://api.highcharts.com/class-reference/Highcharts.Point).
Variables are enclosed in curly brackets. Examples of common
variables to include are `x`, `y`, `series.name` and `series.color`
and other properties on the same form. The `point.key` variable
contains the category name, x value or datetime string depending on
the type of axis. For datetime axes, the `point.key` date format can
be set using `tooltip.xDateFormat`.
In v12+, locale-aware date names follow the browser's casing and can
be lower-case, so use the `ucfirst` helper (for example
`{ucfirst point.key}`) if you want a capitalized header.

name: series-tooltip-nullFormat
title: nullFormat
description:
The HTML of the null point's line in the tooltip. Works analogously
to [pointFormat](#tooltip.pointFormat).

name: series-tooltip-nullFormatter
title: nullFormatter
description:
Callback function to format the text of the tooltip for
visible null points.
Works analogously to [formatter](#tooltip.formatter), including the
`ctx` callback argument added in v12.5.0.

name: series-tooltip-pointFormat
title: pointFormat
description:
The HTML of the point's line in the tooltip. The context is the
[Point class](https://api.highcharts.com/class-reference/Highcharts.Point).
Variables are enclosed in curly brackets. Examples of common
variables to include are `x`, `y`, `series.name` and `series.color`
and other properties on the same form. Furthermore, `y` can be
extended by the `tooltip.valuePrefix` and `tooltip.valueSuffix`
variables. This can also be overridden for each series, which makes
it a good hook for displaying units.

In styled mode, the dot is colored by a class name rather than the
point color.

name: series-tooltip-pointFormatter
title: pointFormatter
description:
A callback function for formatting the HTML output for a single point
in the tooltip. Like the `pointFormat` string, but with more
flexibility. Since v12.6.0, the callback also receives `ctx` as the
first argument, so that arrow functions can access the same context
as regular functions using `this`.

name: series-tooltip-position
title: position
description:
Positioning options for fixed tooltip, taking effect only when
[tooltip.fixed](#tooltip.fixed) is `true`.

name: series-tooltip-position-align
title: align
description: The horizontal alignment of the fixed tooltip.

name: series-tooltip-position-relativeTo
title: relativeTo
description:
What the fixed tooltip alignment should be relative to.

The default, `pane`, means that it is aligned within the plot
area for that given series. If the tooltip is split (as default
in Stock charts), each partial tooltip is aligned within the
series' pane.

name: series-tooltip-position-verticalAlign
title: verticalAlign
description: The vertical alignment of the fixed tooltip.

name: series-tooltip-position-x
title: x
description:
X pixel offset from the given position. Can be used to shy away
from axis lines, grid lines etc to avoid the tooltip overlapping
other elements.

name: series-tooltip-position-y
title: y
description:
Y pixel offset from the given position. Can be used to shy away
from axis lines, grid lines etc to avoid the tooltip overlapping
other elements.

name: series-tooltip-showDelay
title: showDelay
description:
The number of milliseconds to wait until the tooltip is shown when
mouse over a point. Works on initial hover.

name: series-tooltip-valueDecimals
title: valueDecimals
description:
How many decimals to show in each series' y value. This is
overridable in each series' tooltip options object. The default is to
preserve all decimals.

name: series-tooltip-valuePrefix
title: valuePrefix
description:
A string to prepend to each series' y value. Overridable in each
series' tooltip options object.

name: series-tooltip-valueSuffix
title: valueSuffix
description:
A string to append to each series' y value. Overridable in each
series' tooltip options object.

name: series-tooltip-xDateFormat
title: xDateFormat
description:
The format for the date in the tooltip header if the X axis is a
datetime axis. The default is a best guess based on the smallest
distance between points in the chart.

name: series-turboThreshold
title: turboThreshold
description:
When a series contains a `data` array that is longer than this, the
Series class looks for data configurations of plain numbers or arrays of
numbers. The first and last valid points are checked. If found, the rest
of the data is assumed to be the same. This saves expensive data checking
and indexing in long series, and makes data-heavy charts render faster.

Set it to `0` disable.

Note:
- In boost mode turbo threshold is forced. Only array of numbers or two
  dimensional arrays are allowed.
- In version 11.4.3 and earlier, if object configurations were passed
  beyond the turbo threshold, a warning was logged in the console and the
  data series didn't render.

name: series-visible
title: visible
description: Set the initial visibility of the series.

name: series-zIndex
title: zIndex
description: Define the visual z index of the series.

name: series-zoneAxis
title: zoneAxis
description: Defines the Axis on which the zones are applied.

name: series-zones
title: zones
description:
An array defining zones within a series. Zones can be applied to the
X axis, Y axis or Z axis for bubbles, according to the `zoneAxis`
option. The zone definitions have to be in ascending order regarding
to the value.

In styled mode, the color zones are styled with the
`.highcharts-zone-{n}` class, or custom classed from the `className`
option
([view live demo](https://jsfiddle.net/gh/get/library/pure/highcharts/highcharts/tree/master/samples/highcharts/css/color-zones/)).

name: series-zones-className
title: className
description: Styled mode only. A custom class name for the zone.

name: series-zones-color
title: color
description: Defines the color of the series.

name: series-zones-dashStyle
title: dashStyle
description: A name for the dash style to use for the graph.

name: series-zones-fillColor
title: fillColor
description: Defines the fill color for the series (in area type series)

name: series-zones-value
title: value
description:
The value up to where the zone extends, if undefined the zones
stretches to the last value in the series.

name: series-zoomEnabled
title: zoomEnabled
description:
Whether to zoom non-cartesian series. If `chart.zooming` is set, the option
allows to disable zooming on an individual non-cartesian series. By default
zooming is enabled for all series.

**Note**: This option works only for non-cartesian series.

name: series-id
title: id
description:
An id for the series. This can be used after render time to get a pointer
to the series object through `chart.get()`.

name: series-index
title: index
description:
The index of the series in the chart, affecting the internal index in the
`chart.series` array, the visible Z index as well as the order in the
legend.

name: series-legendIndex
title: legendIndex
description: The sequential index of the series in the legend.

name: series-name
title: name
description:
The name of the series as shown in the legend, tooltip etc. If a `dataTable`
and `dataMapping` are used, the name defaults to the id of the primary data
table column. Otherwise, it defaults to "Series {n}", where n is the index of
the series, starting at 1.

name: series-stack
title: stack
description:
This option allows grouping series in a stacked chart. The stack option
can be a string or anything else, as long as the grouped series' stack
options match each other after conversion into a string.

name: series-type
title: type
description:
The type of series, for example `line` or `column`. By default, the
series type is inherited from [chart.type](#chart.type), so unless the
chart is a combination of series types, there is no need to set it on the
series level.

name: series-xAxis
title: xAxis
description:
When using dual or multiple x axes, this number defines which xAxis the
particular series is connected to. It refers to either the
{@link #xAxis.id|axis id}
or the index of the axis in the xAxis array, with 0 being the first.

name: series-yAxis
title: yAxis
description:
When using dual or multiple y axes, this number defines which yAxis the
particular series is connected to. It refers to either the
{@link #yAxis.id|axis id}
or the index of the axis in the yAxis array, with 0 being the first.

name: series-data
title: data
description: The series data, as an array of values, tuples or objects.

name: series<arcdiagram>
title: series<arcdiagram>

name: series<arcdiagram>-data
title: data

name: series<arcdiagram>-data-accessibility
title: accessibility
description: Accessibility options for a data point.

name: series<arcdiagram>-data-accessibility-description
title: description
description: Provide a description of the data point, announced to screen readers.

name: series<arcdiagram>-data-accessibility-enabled
title: enabled
description:
Set to false to disable accessibility functionality for a specific point.
The point will not be included in keyboard navigation, and will not be
exposed to assistive technology.

name: series<arcdiagram>-data-className
title: className
description:
An additional, individual class name for the data point's graphic
representation. Changes to a point's color will also be reflected in a
chart's legend and tooltip.

name: series<arcdiagram>-data-color
title: color
description:
The color for the individual _link_. By default, the link color is the same
as the node it extends from. The `series.fillOpacity` option also applies to
the points, so when setting a specific link color, consider setting the
`fillOpacity` to 1.

name: series<arcdiagram>-data-colorIndex
title: colorIndex
description:
A specific color index to use for the point, so its graphic representations
are given the class name `highcharts-color-{n}`. In styled mode this will
change the color of the graphic. In non-styled mode, the color is set by the
`fill` attribute, so the change in class name won't have a visual effect by
default.

Since v11, CSS variables on the form `--highcharts-color-{n}` make changing
the color scheme very convenient.

name: series<arcdiagram>-data-custom
title: custom
description:
A reserved subspace to store options and values for customized functionality.
Here you can add additional data for your own event callbacks and formatter
callbacks.

name: series<arcdiagram>-data-events
title: events
description: The individual point events.

name: series<arcdiagram>-data-id
title: id
description:
An id for the point. This can be used after render time to get a
pointer to the point object through `chart.get()`.

name: series<arcdiagram>-data-labelrank
title: labelrank
description:
The rank for all this point's data labels in case of collision. If two
data labels are about to overlap, only the one with the highest `labelrank`
will be drawn.

The `labelrank` set on `series.dataLabels` takes precedence over this.

name: series<arcdiagram>-data-name
title: name
description: The name of the point as shown in the legend, tooltip, dataLabels, etc.

name: series<arcdiagram>-data-selected
title: selected
description: Whether the data point is selected initially.

name: series<arcdiagram>-data-from
title: from
description: The node that the link runs from.

name: series<arcdiagram>-data-to
title: to
description: The node that the link runs to.

name: series<arcdiagram>-data-weight
title: weight
description: The weight of the link.

name: series<arcdiagram>-data-linkWeight
title: linkWeight
description:
The link weight, in pixels. If not set, width is calculated per link,
depending on the weight value.

name: series<arcdiagram>-linkRadius
title: linkRadius
description:
The radius of the link arc. If not set, series renders a semi-circle
between the nodes, except when overflowing the edge of the plot area,
in which case an arc touching the edge is rendered. If `linkRadius`
is set, an arc extending to the given value is rendered.

name: series<arcdiagram>-linkWeight
title: linkWeight
description:
The global link weight, in pixels. If not set, width is calculated
per link, depending on the weight value.

name: series<arcdiagram>-nodes
title: nodes
description:
A collection of options for the individual nodes. The nodes in an arc diagram
are auto-generated instances of `Highcharts.Point`, but options can be
applied here and linked by the `id`.

name: series<arcdiagram>-nodes-color
title: color
description: The color of the auto generated node.

name: series<arcdiagram>-nodes-colorIndex
title: colorIndex
description:
The color index of the auto generated node, especially for use in styled
mode.

name: series<arcdiagram>-nodes-dataLabels
title: dataLabels
description:
Individual data label for each node. The options are the same as the ones for
[series.arcdiagram.dataLabels](#series.arcdiagram.dataLabels).

name: series<arcdiagram>-nodes-dataLabels-nodeFormat
title: nodeFormat
description:
The
[format string](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting)
specifying what to show for _nodes_ in the sankey diagram. By
default the `nodeFormatter` returns `{point.name}`.

name: series<arcdiagram>-nodes-dataLabels-nodeFormatter
title: nodeFormatter
description:
Callback to format data labels for _nodes_ in the sankey diagram.
The `nodeFormat` option takes precedence over the
`nodeFormatter`.

name: series<arcdiagram>-nodes-height
title: height
description: The height of the node.

name: series<arcdiagram>-nodes-id
title: id
description:
The id of the auto-generated node, referring to the `from` or `to` setting of
the link.

name: series<arcdiagram>-nodes-name
title: name
description:
The name to display for the node in data labels and tooltips. Use this when
the name is different from the `id`. Where the id must be unique for each
node, this is not necessary for the name.

name: series<arcdiagram>-nodes-offsetHorizontal
title: offsetHorizontal
description:
The horizontal offset of a node. Positive values shift the node right,
negative shift it left.

If a percentage string is given, the node is offset by the percentage of the
node size.

name: series<arcdiagram>-nodes-offsetVertical
title: offsetVertical
description:
The vertical offset of a node. Positive values shift the node down,
negative shift it up.

If a percentage string is given, the node is offset by the percentage of the
node size.

name: series<arcdiagram>-offset
title: offset
description:
The offset of an arc diagram nodes column in relation to the
`plotArea`. The offset equal to 50% places nodes in the center of a
chart. By default the series is placed so that the biggest node is
touching the bottom border of the `plotArea`.

name: series<area>
title: series<area>

name: series<area>-data
title: data
description:
An array of data points for the series. For the `area` series type,
points can be given in the following ways:

1. An array of numerical values. In this case, the numerical values will be
   interpreted as `y` options. The `x` values will be automatically
   calculated, either starting at 0 and incremented by 1, or from
   `pointStart` * and `pointInterval` given in the series options. If the
   axis has categories, these will be used. Example:
   ```js
   data: [0, 5, 3, 5]
   ```

2. An array of arrays with 2 values. In this case, the values correspond to
   `x,y`. If the first value is a string, it is applied as the name of the
   point, and the `x` value is inferred.
   ```js
   data: [
       [0, 9],
       [1, 7],
       [2, 6]
   ]
   ```

3. An array of objects with named values. The following snippet shows only a
   few settings, see the complete options set below. If the total number of
   data points exceeds the series'
   [turboThreshold](#series.area.turboThreshold), this option is not
   available.
   ```js
   data: [{
       x: 1,
       y: 9,
       name: "Point2",
       color: "#00FF00"
   }, {
       x: 1,
       y: 6,
       name: "Point1",
       color: "#FF00FF"
   }]
   ```

name: series<arearange>
title: series<arearange>

name: series<arearange>-data
title: data
description:
An array of data points for the series. For the `arearange` series type,
points can be given in the following ways:

1.  An array of arrays with 3 or 2 values. In this case, the values
    correspond to `x,low,high`. If the first value is a string, it is
    applied as the name of the point, and the `x` value is inferred.
    The `x` value can also be omitted, in which case the inner arrays
    should be of length 2\. Then the `x` value is automatically calculated,
    either starting at 0 and incremented by 1, or from `pointStart`
    and `pointInterval` given in the series options.
    ```js
    data: [
        [0, 8, 3],
        [1, 1, 1],
        [2, 6, 8]
    ]
    ```

2.  An array of objects with named values. The following snippet shows only a
    few settings, see the complete options set below. If the total number of
    data points exceeds the series'
    [turboThreshold](#series.arearange.turboThreshold),
    this option is not available.
    ```js
    data: [{
        x: 1,
        low: 9,
        high: 0,
        name: "Point2",
        color: "#00FF00"
    }, {
        x: 1,
        low: 3,
        high: 4,
        name: "Point1",
        color: "#FF00FF"
    }]
    ```

name: series<arearange>-data-high
title: high
description: The high or maximum value for each data point.

name: series<arearange>-data-low
title: low
description: The low or minimum value for each data point.

name: series<areaspline>
title: series<areaspline>

name: series<areaspline>-data
title: data
description:
An array of data points for the series. For the `areaspline` series
type, points can be given in the following ways:

1. An array of numerical values. In this case, the numerical values will be
   interpreted as `y` options. The `x` values will be automatically
   calculated, either starting at 0 and incremented by 1, or from
   `pointStart` and `pointInterval` given in the series options. If the axis

to place it next to the preceding node. Note that this option name is

rendered top down. In this case the "columns" are horizontal.

title: height

title: id

to place it next to the preceding node. Alias of `nodes.column`, but in

negative shift it left.

If a percentage string is given, the node is offset by the percentage of the
node size.

negative shift it up.

If a percentage string is given, the node is offset by the percentage of the
node size.

name: series<variwide>-data
title: data
description:
An array of data points for the series. For the `variwide` series type,
points can be given in the following ways:

1. An array of arrays with 3 or 2 values. In this case, the values correspond
   to `x,y,z`. If the first value is a string, it is applied as the name of
   the point, and the `x` value is inferred. The `x` value can also be
   omitted, in which case the inner arrays should be of length 2. Then the
   `x` value is automatically calculated, either starting at 0 and
   incremented by 1, or from `pointStart` and `pointInterval` given in the
   series options.
   ```js
      data: [
          [0, 1, 2],
          [1, 5, 5],
          [2, 0, 2]
      ]
   ```

2. An array of objects with named values. The following snippet shows only a
   few settings, see the complete options set below. If the total number of
   data points exceeds the series'
   [turboThreshold](#series.variwide.turboThreshold), this option is not
   available.
   ```js
      data: [{
          x: 1,
          y: 1,
          z: 1,
          name: "Point2",
          color: "#00FF00"
      }, {
          x: 1,
          y: 5,
          z: 4,
          name: "Point1",
          color: "#FF00FF"
      }]
   ```

name: series<variwide>-data-z
title: z
description:
The relative width for each column. On a category axis, the widths are
distributed so they sum up to the X axis length. On linear and datetime axes,
the columns will be laid out from the X value and Z units along the axis.

name: series<vector>
title: series<vector>

name: series<vector>-data
title: data
description:
An array of data points for the series. For the `vector` series type,
points can be given in the following ways:

1. An array of arrays with 4 values. In this case, the values correspond to
   to `x,y,length,direction`. If the first value is a string, it is applied
   as the name of the point, and the `x` value is inferred.
   ```js
   data: [
       [0, 0, 10, 90],
       [0, 1, 5, 180],
       [1, 1, 2, 270]
   ]
   ```

2. An array of objects with named values. The following snippet shows only a
   few settings, see the complete options set below. If the total number of
   data points exceeds the series'
   [turboThreshold](#series.area.turboThreshold), this option is not
   available.
   ```js
   data: [{
       x: 0,
       y: 0,
       name: "Point2",
       length: 10,
       direction: 90
   }, {
       x: 1,
       y: 1,
       name: "Point1",
       direction: 270
   }]
   ```

name: series<vector>-data-direction
title: direction
description: The vector direction in degrees, where 0 is north (pointing towards south).

name: series<vector>-data-length

The length of the vector. The rendered length will relate to the
`vectorLength` setting.

   ```js
   data: [
       [0, 7],
       [1, 8],
       [2, 3]
   ]
   ```

3. An array of objects with named values. The following snippet shows only a
   few settings, see the complete options set below. If the total number of
   data points exceeds the series'
   [turboThreshold](#series.waterfall.turboThreshold), this option is not
   available.
   ```js
   data: [{
       x: 1,
       y: 8,
       name: "Point2",
       color: "#00FF00"
   }, {
       x: 1,
       y: 8,
       name: "Point1",
       color: "#FF00FF"
   }]
   ```

name: series<waterfall>-data-isIntermediateSum

the values added or subtracted since the last intermediate sum,
or since the start of the series. The `y` value is ignored.

name: series<waterfall>-data-isSum
title: isSum
description:

the entire series. The `y` value is ignored.

name: series<xrange>-data-partialFill-fill

of the point color.

name: series<xrange>-data-x

name: series<xrange>-data-x2

name: series<xrange>-data-y

name: sonification-afterSeriesWait
title: afterSeriesWait
description:
The time to wait in milliseconds after each data series when playing
the series one after the other.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions
title: defaultInstrumentOptions
description:
Default sonification options for all instrument tracks.

If specific options are also set on individual tracks or per
series, those will override these options.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-activeWhen
title: activeWhen
description:
Define a condition for when a track should be active and not.

Can either be a function callback or a configuration object.

If a function is used, it should return a `boolean` for whether
or not the track should be active. The function is called for
each audio event, and receives a parameter object with `time`,
and potentially `point` and `value` properties depending on the
track. `point` is available if the audio event is related to a
data point. `value` is available if the track is used as a
context track, and `valueInterval` is used.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-activeWhen-crossingDown
title: crossingDown
description:
Track is only active when `prop` was above, and is now at or
below this value.

If both `crossingUp` and `crossingDown` are defined, the track
is active if either condition is met.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-activeWhen-crossingUp
title: crossingUp
description:
Track is only active when `prop` was below, and is now at or
above this value.

If both `crossingUp` and `crossingDown` are defined, the track
is active if either condition is met.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-activeWhen-max
title: max
description: Track is only active when `prop` is below or at this value.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-activeWhen-min
title: min
description: Track is only active when `prop` is above or at this value.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-activeWhen-prop
title: prop
description: The point property to compare, for example `y` or `x`.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-instrument
title: instrument
description:
Instrument to use for playing.

Can either be a string referencing a synth preset, or it can be
a synth configuration object.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping
title: mapping
description:
Mapping options for the audio parameters.

All parameters can be either:
 - A string, referencing a point property to map to.
 - A number, setting the value of the audio parameter directly.
 - A callback function, returning the value programmatically.
 - An object defining detailed configuration of the mapping.

If a function is used, it should return the desired value for
the audio parameter. The function is called for each audio event
to be played, and receives a context object parameter with
`time`, and potentially `point` and `value` depending on the
track. `point` is available if the audio event is related to a
data point, and `value` is available if the track is used for a
context track using `valueInterval`.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-frequency
title: frequency
description: Frequency in Hertz of notes. Overrides pitch mapping if set.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-gapBetweenNotes
title: gapBetweenNotes
description:
Gap in milliseconds between notes if pitch is mapped to an
array of notes.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-highpass
title: highpass
description:
Mapping options for the highpass filter.

A highpass filter lets high frequencies through, but stops
low frequencies, making the sound thinner.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-highpass-frequency
title: frequency
description: Map to filter frequency in Hertz from 1 to 20,000Hz.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-highpass-resonance
title: resonance
description:
Map to filter resonance in dB. Can be negative to cause a
dip, or positive to cause a bump.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-lowpass
title: lowpass
description:
Mapping options for the lowpass filter.

A lowpass filter lets low frequencies through, but stops high
frequencies, making the sound more dull.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-lowpass-frequency
title: frequency
description: Map to filter frequency in Hertz from 1 to 20,000Hz.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-lowpass-resonance
title: resonance
description:
Map to filter resonance in dB. Can be negative to cause a
dip, or positive to cause a bump.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-noteDuration
title: noteDuration
description:
Note duration determines for how long a note plays, in
milliseconds.

It only affects instruments that are able to play
continuous sustained notes. Examples of these instruments
from the presets include `flute`, `saxophone`, `trumpet`,
`sawsynth`, `wobble`, `basic1`, `basic2`, `sine`,
`sineGlide`, `triangle`, `square`, `sawtooth`, `noise`,
`filteredNoise`, and `wind`.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-pan
title: pan
description:
Pan refers to the stereo panning position of the sound.
It is defined from -1 (left) to 1 (right).

By default it is mapped to `x`, making the sound move from
left to right as the chart plays.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-pitch
title: pitch
description:
Musical pitch refers to how high or low notes are played.

By default it is mapped to `y` so low `y` values are played
with a lower pitch, and high values are played with a higher
pitch.

Pitch mapping has a few extra features compared to other
audio parameters.

Firstly, it accepts not only number values, but also string
values denoting note names. These are given in the form
`<note><octave>`, for example `"c6"` or `"F#2"`.

Secondly, it is possible to map pitch to an array of notes.
In this case, the `[gapBetweenNotes](#sonification.defaultInstrumentOptions.mapping.gapBetweenNotes)`
mapping determines the delay between these notes.

Thirdly, it is possible to define a musical scale to follow
when mapping.

Can be set to a fixed value, an array, a prop to map to, a
function, or a mapping object.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-pitch-scale
title: scale
description:
Map pitches to a musical scale. The scale is defined as an
array of semitone offsets from the root note.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-playDelay
title: playDelay
description:
Milliseconds to wait before playing, comes in addition to
the time determined by the `time` mapping.

Can also be negative to play before the mapped time.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-time
title: time
description:
Time mapping determines what time each point plays. It is
defined as an offset in milliseconds, where 0 means it
plays immediately when the chart is sonified.

By default time is mapped to `x`, meaning points with the
lowest `x` value plays first, and points with the highest
`x` value plays last.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-time-mapFunction
title: mapFunction
description: How to perform the mapping.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-time-mapTo
title: mapTo
description:
A point property to map the mapping parameter to.

A negative sign `-` can be placed before the property name
to make mapping inverted.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-time-max
title: max
description:
The maximum value for the audio parameter. This is the
highest value the audio parameter will be mapped to.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-time-min
title: min
description:
The minimum value for the audio parameter. This is the
lowest value the audio parameter will be mapped to.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-time-value
title: value
description:
A fixed value to use for the prop when mapping.

For example, if mapping to `y`, setting value to `4` will
map as if all points had a y value of 4.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-time-within
title: within
description:
What data values to map the parameter within.

Mapping within `"series"` will make the lowest value point
in the series map to the min audio parameter value, and the
highest value will map to the max audio parameter.

Mapping within `"chart"` will make the lowest value point in
the whole chart map to the min audio parameter value, and
the highest value in the whole chart will map to the max
audio parameter.

You can also map within the X or Y axis of each series.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-tremolo
title: tremolo
description:
Mapping options for tremolo effects.

Tremolo is repeated changes of volume over time.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-tremolo-depth
title: depth
description:
Map to tremolo depth, from 0 to 1.

This determines the intensity of the tremolo effect, how
much the volume changes.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-tremolo-speed
title: speed
description:
Map to tremolo speed, from 0 to 1.

This determines the speed of the tremolo effect, how fast
the volume changes.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-volume
title: volume
description: The volume of notes, from 0 to 1.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-midiName
title: midiName
description:
Name to use for a track when exporting to MIDI.
By default it uses the series name if the track is related to
a series.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-pointGrouping
title: pointGrouping
description: Options for point grouping, specifically for instrument tracks.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-pointGrouping-algorithm
title: algorithm
description:
The grouping algorithm, deciding which points to keep when
grouping a set of points together. By default `"minmax"` is
used, which keeps both the minimum and maximum points.

The other algorithms will either keep the first point in the
group (time wise), last point, middle point, or both the first
and the last point.

The timing of the resulting point(s) is then adjusted to play
evenly, regardless of its original position within the group.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-pointGrouping-enabled
title: enabled
description: Whether or not to group points

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-pointGrouping-groupTimespan
title: groupTimespan
description:
The size of each group in milliseconds. Audio events closer than
this are grouped together.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-pointGrouping-prop
title: prop
description:
The data property for each point to compare when deciding which
points to keep in the group.

By default it is "y", which means that if the `"minmax"`
algorithm is used, the two points the group with the lowest and
highest `y` value will be kept, and the others not played.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-roundToMusicalNotes
title: roundToMusicalNotes
description:
Round pitch mapping to musical notes.

If `false`, will play the exact mapped note, even if it is out
of tune compared to the musical notes as defined by 440Hz
standard tuning.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-showPlayMarker
title: showPlayMarker
description: Show play marker (tooltip and/or crosshair) for a track.

name: sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-type
title: type
description:
Type of track. Always `"instrument"` for instrument tracks, and
`"speech"` for speech tracks.

name: sonification-defaultSpeechOptions-pointGrouping-enabled
title: enabled
description: Whether or not to group points

name: sonification-defaultSpeechOptions-pointGrouping-groupTimespan
title: groupTimespan
description:
The size of each group in milliseconds. Audio events closer than
this are grouped together.

name: sonification-defaultSpeechOptions-pointGrouping-prop
title: prop
description:
The data property for each point to compare when deciding which
points to keep in the group.

algorithm is used, the two points the group with the lowest and
highest `y` value will be kept, and the others not played.

name: sonification-defaultSpeechOptions-showPlayMarker
title: showPlayMarker
description: Show play marker (tooltip and/or crosshair) for a track.

name: sonification-defaultSpeechOptions-type
title: type
description:
Type of track. Always `"instrument"` for instrument tracks, and
`"speech"` for speech tracks.

name: sonification-defaultSpeechOptions-language
title: language
description:
The language to speak in for speech tracks, as an IETF BCP 47
language tag.

name: sonification-defaultSpeechOptions-preferredVoice
title: preferredVoice
description:
Name of the voice synthesis to prefer for speech tracks.

If not available, falls back to the default voice for the
selected language.

Different platforms provide different voices for web speech
synthesis.

name: sonification-duration
title: duration
description: The total duration of the sonification, in milliseconds.

name: sonification-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable sonification functionality for the chart.

name: sonification-events
title: events
description: Set up event handlers for the sonification

name: sonification-events-afterUpdate
title: afterUpdate
description:
Called after updating the sonification.

A context object is passed to the function, with properties `chart`
and `timeline`.

name: sonification-events-beforePlay
title: beforePlay
description:
Called immediately when a play is requested.

A context object is passed to the function, with properties `chart`
and `timeline`.

name: sonification-events-beforeUpdate
title: beforeUpdate
description:
Called before updating the sonification.

A context object is passed to the function, with properties `chart`
and `timeline`.

name: sonification-events-onBoundaryHit
title: onBoundaryHit
description:
Called when attempting to play an adjacent point or series, and
there is none.

By default a percussive sound is played.

A context object is passed to the function, with properties `chart`,
`timeline`, and `attemptedNext`. `attemptedNext` is a boolean
property that is `true` if the boundary hit was from trying to play
the next series/point, and `false` if it was from trying to play the
previous.

name: sonification-events-onEnd
title: onEnd
description:
Called when play is completed.

A context object is passed to the function, with properties `chart`,
`timeline` and `pointsPlayed`. `pointsPlayed` is an array of `Point`
objects, referencing data points that were related to the audio
events played.

name: sonification-events-onPlay
title: onPlay
description:
Called on play.

A context object is passed to the function, with properties `chart`
and `timeline`.

name: sonification-events-onSeriesEnd
title: onSeriesEnd
description:
Called when finished playing a series.

A context object is passed to the function, with properties `series`
and `timeline`.

name: sonification-events-onSeriesStart
title: onSeriesStart
description:
Called on the beginning of playing a series.

A context object is passed to the function, with properties `series`
and `timeline`.

name: sonification-events-onStop
title: onStop
description:
Called on pause, cancel, or if play is completed.

A context object is passed to the function, with properties `chart`,
`timeline` and `pointsPlayed`. `pointsPlayed` is an array of `Point`
objects, referencing data points that were related to the audio
events played.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks
title: globalContextTracks
description:
Context tracks to add globally, an array of either instrument
tracks, speech tracks, or a mix.

Context tracks are not tied to data points, but play at a set
interval - either based on time or on prop values.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-activeWhen
title: activeWhen
description:
Define a condition for when a track should be active and not.

Can either be a function callback or a configuration object.

If a function is used, it should return a `boolean` for whether
or not the track should be active. The function is called for
each audio event, and receives a parameter object with `time`,
and potentially `point` and `value` properties depending on the
track. `point` is available if the audio event is related to a
data point. `value` is available if the track is used as a
context track, and `valueInterval` is used.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-activeWhen-crossingDown
title: crossingDown
description:
Track is only active when `prop` was above, and is now at or
below this value.

If both `crossingUp` and `crossingDown` are defined, the track
is active if either condition is met.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-activeWhen-crossingUp
title: crossingUp
description:
Track is only active when `prop` was below, and is now at or
above this value.

If both `crossingUp` and `crossingDown` are defined, the track
is active if either condition is met.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-activeWhen-max
title: max
description: Track is only active when `prop` is below or at this value.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-activeWhen-min
title: min
description: Track is only active when `prop` is above or at this value.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-activeWhen-prop
title: prop
description: The point property to compare, for example `y` or `x`.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-instrument
title: instrument
description:
Instrument to use for playing.

Can either be a string referencing a synth preset, or it can be
a synth configuration object.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-frequency
title: frequency
description: Frequency in Hertz of notes. Overrides pitch mapping if set.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-gapBetweenNotes
title: gapBetweenNotes
description:
Gap in milliseconds between notes if pitch is mapped to an
array of notes.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-highpass
title: highpass
description:
Mapping options for the highpass filter.

A highpass filter lets high frequencies through, but stops
low frequencies, making the sound thinner.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-highpass-frequency
title: frequency
description: Map to filter frequency in Hertz from 1 to 20,000Hz.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-highpass-resonance
title: resonance
description:
Map to filter resonance in dB. Can be negative to cause a
dip, or positive to cause a bump.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-lowpass
title: lowpass
description:
Mapping options for the lowpass filter.

A lowpass filter lets low frequencies through, but stops high
frequencies, making the sound more dull.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-lowpass-frequency
title: frequency
description: Map to filter frequency in Hertz from 1 to 20,000Hz.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-lowpass-resonance
title: resonance
description:
Map to filter resonance in dB. Can be negative to cause a
dip, or positive to cause a bump.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-noteDuration
title: noteDuration
description:
Note duration determines for how long a note plays, in
milliseconds.

It only affects instruments that are able to play
continuous sustained notes. Examples of these instruments
from the presets include `flute`, `saxophone`, `trumpet`,
`sawsynth`, `wobble`, `basic1`, `basic2`, `sine`,
`sineGlide`, `triangle`, `square`, `sawtooth`, `noise`,
`filteredNoise`, and `wind`.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-pan
title: pan
description:
Pan refers to the stereo panning position of the sound.
It is defined from -1 (left) to 1 (right).

By default it is mapped to `x`, making the sound move from
left to right as the chart plays.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-pitch
title: pitch
description:
Musical pitch refers to how high or low notes are played.

By default it is mapped to `y` so low `y` values are played
with a lower pitch, and high values are played with a higher
pitch.

Pitch mapping has a few extra features compared to other
audio parameters.

Firstly, it accepts not only number values, but also string
values denoting note names. These are given in the form
`<note><octave>`, for example `"c6"` or `"F#2"`.

Secondly, it is possible to map pitch to an array of notes.
In this case, the `[gapBetweenNotes](#sonification.defaultInstrumentOptions.mapping.gapBetweenNotes)`
mapping determines the delay between these notes.

Thirdly, it is possible to define a musical scale to follow
when mapping.

Can be set to a fixed value, an array, a prop to map to, a
function, or a mapping object.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-pitch-scale
title: scale
description:
Map pitches to a musical scale. The scale is defined as an
array of semitone offsets from the root note.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-playDelay
title: playDelay
description:
Milliseconds to wait before playing, comes in addition to
the time determined by the `time` mapping.

Can also be negative to play before the mapped time.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-time
title: time
description:
Time mapping determines what time each point plays. It is
defined as an offset in milliseconds, where 0 means it
plays immediately when the chart is sonified.

By default time is mapped to `x`, meaning points with the
lowest `x` value plays first, and points with the highest
`x` value plays last.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-time-mapFunction
title: mapFunction
description: How to perform the mapping.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-time-mapTo
title: mapTo
description:
A point property to map the mapping parameter to.

A negative sign `-` can be placed before the property name
to make mapping inverted.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-time-max
title: max
description:
The maximum value for the audio parameter. This is the
highest value the audio parameter will be mapped to.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-time-min
title: min
description:
The minimum value for the audio parameter. This is the
lowest value the audio parameter will be mapped to.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-time-value
title: value
description:
A fixed value to use for the prop when mapping.

For example, if mapping to `y`, setting value to `4` will
map as if all points had a y value of 4.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-time-within
title: within
description:
What data values to map the parameter within.

Mapping within `"series"` will make the lowest value point
in the series map to the min audio parameter value, and the
highest value will map to the max audio parameter.

Mapping within `"chart"` will make the lowest value point in
the whole chart map to the min audio parameter value, and
the highest value in the whole chart will map to the max
audio parameter.

You can also map within the X or Y axis of each series.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-tremolo
title: tremolo
description:
Mapping options for tremolo effects.

Tremolo is repeated changes of volume over time.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-tremolo-depth
title: depth
description:
Map to tremolo depth, from 0 to 1.

This determines the intensity of the tremolo effect, how
much the volume changes.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-tremolo-speed
title: speed
description:
Map to tremolo speed, from 0 to 1.

This determines the speed of the tremolo effect, how fast
the volume changes.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-volume
title: volume
description: The volume of notes, from 0 to 1.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-rate
title: rate
description: Rate mapping for speech tracks.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-rate-mapFunction
title: mapFunction
description: How to perform the mapping.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-rate-mapTo
title: mapTo
description:

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-rate-max

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-rate-min
title: min

lowest value the audio parameter will be mapped to.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-mapping-text
title: text
description: Text mapping for speech tracks.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-midiName
title: midiName
description:
Name to use for a track when exporting to MIDI.
By default it uses the series name if the track is related to
a series.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-pointGrouping
title: pointGrouping
description: Options for point grouping, specifically for instrument tracks.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-pointGrouping-algorithm
title: algorithm
description:
The grouping algorithm, deciding which points to keep when
grouping a set of points together. By default `"minmax"` is
used, which keeps both the minimum and maximum points.

The other algorithms will either keep the first point in the
group (time wise), last point, middle point, or both the first
and the last point.

The timing of the resulting point(s) is then adjusted to play
evenly, regardless of its original position within the group.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-pointGrouping-enabled
title: enabled
description: Whether or not to group points

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-pointGrouping-groupTimespan
title: groupTimespan
description:
The size of each group in milliseconds. Audio events closer than
this are grouped together.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-pointGrouping-prop

description:

points to keep in the group.

By default it is "y", which means that if the `"minmax"`
algorithm is used, the two points the group with the lowest and
highest `y` value will be kept, and the others not played.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-roundToMusicalNotes
title: roundToMusicalNotes
description:
Round pitch mapping to musical notes.

If `false`, will play the exact mapped note, even if it is out
of tune compared to the musical notes as defined by 440Hz
standard tuning.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-showPlayMarker
title: showPlayMarker
description: Show play marker (tooltip and/or crosshair) for a track.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-type
title: type
description:
Type of track. Always `"instrument"` for instrument tracks, and
`"speech"` for speech tracks.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-timeInterval
title: timeInterval
description:
Set a context track to play periodically every `timeInterval`
milliseconds while the sonification is playing.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-valueInterval
title: valueInterval
description:

playing.

For example, setting `valueProp` to `x` and `valueInterval` to 5

prop value relative to the min/max values for that prop.

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-valueMapFunction

name: sonification-globalContextTracks-valueProp
title: valueProp
description: The point property to play context for when using `valueInterval`.

name: sonification-globalTracks-type
title: type
description:
Type of track. Always `"instrument"` for instrument tracks, and
`"speech"` for speech tracks.

name: sonification-masterVolume
title: masterVolume
description: Overall/master volume for the sonification, from 0 to 1.

name: sonification-order
title: order
description:
What order to play the data series in, either `sequential` where
the series play individually one after the other, or `simultaneous`
where the series play all at once.

name: sonification-pointGrouping
title: pointGrouping
description:
Options for grouping data points together when sonifying. This
allows for the visual presentation to contain more points than what
is being played. If not enabled, all visible / uncropped points are
played.

name: sonification-pointGrouping-algorithm
title: algorithm
description:
The grouping algorithm, deciding which points to keep when
grouping a set of points together. By default `"minmax"` is
used, which keeps both the minimum and maximum points.

The other algorithms will either keep the first point in the
group (time wise), last point, middle point, or both the first
and the last point.

The timing of the resulting point(s) is then adjusted to play
evenly, regardless of its original position within the group.

name: sonification-pointGrouping-enabled
title: enabled
description: Whether or not to group points

name: sonification-pointGrouping-groupTimespan
title: groupTimespan
description:
The size of each group in milliseconds. Audio events closer than
this are grouped together.

name: sonification-pointGrouping-prop
title: prop
description:
The data property for each point to compare when deciding which
points to keep in the group.

By default it is "y", which means that if the `"minmax"`
algorithm is used, the two points the group with the lowest and
highest `y` value will be kept, and the others not played.

name: sonification-showCrosshair
title: showCrosshair
description:
Show X and Y axis crosshairs (if they exist) as the chart plays.

Note that if multiple tracks that play at different times try to
show the crosshairs, it can be glitchy, so it is recommended in
those cases to turn this on/off for individual tracks using the
[showPlayMarker](#plotOptions.series.sonification.tracks.showPlayMarker)
option.

name: sonification-showTooltip
title: showTooltip
description:
Show tooltip as the chart plays.

Note that if multiple tracks that play at different times try to
show the tooltip, it can be glitchy, so it is recommended in
those cases to turn this on/off for individual tracks using the
[showPlayMarker](#plotOptions.series.sonification.tracks.showPlayMarker)
option.

name: sonification-updateInterval
title: updateInterval
description:
How long to wait between each recomputation of the sonification, if
the chart updates rapidly. This avoids slowing down processes like
panning. Given in milliseconds.

name: subtitle
title: subtitle
description:
The chart's subtitle. This can be used both to display a subtitle below
the main title, and to display random text anywhere in the chart. The
subtitle can be updated after chart initialization through the
`Chart.setTitle` method.

name: subtitle-align
title: align
description:
The horizontal alignment of the subtitle. Can be one of "left",
"center" and "right". Since v12, it defaults to `undefined`, meaning
the actual alignment is inherited from the alignment of the main
title.

name: subtitle-className
title: className
description:
A CSS class name to apply to the subtitle's container div,
allowing unique CSS styling for each chart.

name: subtitle-floating
title: floating
description:
When the subtitle is floating, the plot area will not move to make
space for it.

name: subtitle-style
title: style
description:
CSS styles for the title.

In styled mode, the subtitle style is given in the
`.highcharts-subtitle` class.

name: subtitle-text
title: text
description: The subtitle of the chart.

name: subtitle-useHTML
title: useHTML
description:
Whether to
[use HTML](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting#html)
to render the text.

name: subtitle-verticalAlign
title: verticalAlign
description:
The vertical alignment of the title. Can be one of `"top"`,
`"middle"` and `"bottom"`. When middle, the subtitle behaves as
floating.

name: subtitle-x
title: x
description:
The x position of the subtitle relative to the alignment within
`chart.spacingLeft` and `chart.spacingRight`.

name: subtitle-y
title: y
description:
The y position of the subtitle relative to the alignment within
`chart.spacingTop` and `chart.spacingBottom`. By default the subtitle
is laid out below the title unless the title is floating.

name: time
title: time

name: time-Date
title: Date
description:
A custom `Date` class for advanced date handling. For example,
[JDate](https://github.com/tahajahangir/jdate) can be hooked in to
handle Jalali dates.

name: time-timezone
title: timezone
description:
A named time zone. Supported time zone names rely on the browser
implementations, as described in the [mdn
docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl/DateTimeFormat/DateTimeFormat#timezone).
If the given time zone is not recognized by the browser, Highcharts
provides a warning and falls back to returning a 0 offset,
corresponding to the UTC time zone.

The time zone affects axis scaling, tickmark placement and
time display in `Highcharts.dateFormat`.

Setting `timezone` to `undefined` falls back to the default browser
timezone setting.

Until v11.2.0, this option depended on moment.js.

name: title
title: title
description: The chart's main title.

name: title-align
title: align
description:
The horizontal alignment of the title. Can be one of "left", "center"
and "right".

Since v12 it defaults to `undefined`, meaning the alignment is
computed for best fit. If the text fits in one line, it aligned to
the center, but if it is wrapped into multiple lines, it is aligned
to the left.

name: title-className
title: className
description:
A CSS class name to apply to the title's container div,
allowing unique CSS styling for each chart.

name: title-floating
title: floating
description:
When the title is floating, the plot area will not move to make space
for it.

name: title-margin
title: margin
description:
The margin between the title and the plot area, or if a subtitle
is present, the margin between the subtitle and the plot area.

name: title-minScale
title: minScale
description:
When the title is too wide to fit in the chart, the default behavior
is to scale it down to fit, or apply word wrap if it is scaled down
to `minScale` and still doesn't fit.

The default value reflects the scale, when using default font sizes,
when the title font size matches that of the subtitle. The title
still stands out as it is bold by default.

Set `minScale` to 1 to avoid downscaling.

name: title-style
title: style
description:
CSS styles for the title. Use this for font styling, but use `align`,
`x` and `y` for text alignment.

Note that the default [title.minScale](#title.minScale) option also
affects the rendered font size. In order to keep the font size fixed
regardless of title length, set `minScale` to 1.

In styled mode, the title style is given in the `.highcharts-title`
class.

name: title-text
title: text
description:
The title of the chart. To disable the title, set the `text` to
`undefined`.

name: title-useHTML
title: useHTML
description:
Whether to
[use HTML](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting#html)
to render the text.

name: title-verticalAlign
title: verticalAlign
description:
The vertical alignment of the title. Can be one of `"top"`,
`"middle"` and `"bottom"`. When a value is given, the title behaves
as if [floating](#title.floating) were `true`.

name: title-x
title: x
description:
The x position of the title relative to the alignment within
`chart.spacingLeft` and `chart.spacingRight`.

name: title-y
title: y
description:
The y position of the title relative to the alignment within
[chart.spacingTop](#chart.spacingTop) and [chart.spacingBottom](#chart.spacingBottom). By default it depends on the font size.

name: tooltip
title: tooltip
description:
Options for the tooltip that appears when the user hovers over a
series or point.

name: tooltip-animation
title: animation
description: Enable or disable animation of the tooltip.

name: tooltip-backgroundColor
title: backgroundColor
description:
The background color or gradient for the tooltip.

In styled mode, the stroke width is set in the
`.highcharts-tooltip-box` class.

name: tooltip-borderColor
title: borderColor
description:
The color of the tooltip border. When `undefined` or `null`, the
border takes the color of the corresponding series or point.

By default, in light mode the border color matches the background
color because the shadow makes the tooltip stand out. In dark mode, a
visible line is used because the default shadow is too dark to be
visible on a dark background.

name: tooltip-borderRadius
title: borderRadius
description: The radius of the rounded border corners.

name: tooltip-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description:
The pixel width of the tooltip border. Defaults to 1, but with a
`borderColor` to match the background in light mode, and a visible
lighter border in dark mode.

In styled mode, the stroke width is set in the
`.highcharts-tooltip-box` class.

name: tooltip-className
title: className
description:
A CSS class name to apply to the tooltip, allowing unique CSS
styling for each chart.

**Note:** The class is applied to the SVG element of the tooltip
(the tooltip label group), not to a container div. This allows you
to style the tooltip using CSS applicable to SVG elements.

When [tooltip.outside](#tooltip.outside) is `true`, a separate
container div with class `highcharts-tooltip-container` is created
as the parent to the SVG tooltip element, but the `className` option
is still applied to the SVG element itself, not to the container.

name: tooltip-clusterFormat
title: clusterFormat
description:
The HTML of the cluster point's in the tooltip. Works only with
marker-clusters module and analogously to
[pointFormat](#tooltip.pointFormat).

The cluster tooltip can be also formatted using
`tooltip.formatter` callback function and `point.isCluster` flag.

name: tooltip-dateTimeLabelFormats
title: dateTimeLabelFormats
description:
For series on datetime axes, the date format in the tooltip's
header will by default be guessed based on the closest data points.
This member gives the default string representations used for
each unit. For an overview of the string or object configuration, see
[dateFormat](/class-reference/Highcharts.Time#dateFormat).

name: tooltip-distance
title: distance
description: Distance from point to tooltip in pixels.

name: tooltip-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable or disable the tooltip.

name: tooltip-fixed
title: fixed
description:
Whether the tooltip should be fixed to one position in the chart, or
located next to the point or mouse. When the tooltip is fixed, the
position can be further specified with the
[tooltip.position](#tooltip.position) options set.

name: tooltip-followPointer
title: followPointer
description:
Whether the tooltip should follow the mouse as it moves across
columns, pie slices and other point types with an extent.
By default it behaves this way for pie, polygon, map, sankey
and wordcloud series by override in the `plotOptions`
for those series types.

Does not apply if [split](#tooltip.split) is `true`.

For touch moves to behave the same way, [followTouchMove](#tooltip.followTouchMove) must be `true` also.

name: tooltip-followTouchMove
title: followTouchMove
description:
Whether the tooltip should update as the finger moves on a touch
device. If this is `true` and [chart.panning](#chart.panning) is
set,`followTouchMove` will take over one-finger touches, so the user
needs to use two fingers for zooming and panning.

Note the difference to [followPointer](#tooltip.followPointer) that
only defines the _position_ of the tooltip. If `followPointer` is
false in for example a column series, the tooltip will show above or
below the column, but as `followTouchMove` is true, the tooltip will
jump from column to column as the user swipes across the plot area.

name: tooltip-footerFormat
title: footerFormat
description: A string to append to the tooltip format.

name: tooltip-format
title: format
description:
A [format string](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting)
for the whole shared tooltip. When format strings are a requirement,
it is usually more convenient to use `headerFormat`, `pointFormat`
and `footerFormat`, but the `format` option allows combining them
into one setting.

The context of the format string is the same as that of the
`tooltip.formatter` callback.

name: tooltip-formatter
title: formatter
description:
Callback function to format the text of the tooltip from scratch. In
case of single or [shared](#tooltip.shared) tooltips, a string should
be returned. In case of [split](#tooltip.split) tooltips, it should
return an array where the first item is the header, and subsequent
items are mapped to the points. Return `false` to disable tooltip for
a specific point on series.

A subset of HTML is supported. Unless `useHTML` is true, the HTML of
the tooltip is parsed and converted to SVG, therefore this isn't a
complete HTML renderer. The following HTML tags are supported: `b`,
`br`, `em`, `i`, `span`, `strong`. Spans can be styled with a `style`
attribute, but only text-related CSS, that is shared with SVG, is
handled.

The context of the formatter (since v12) is the
[Point](https://api.highcharts.com/class-reference/Highcharts.Point)
instance. If the tooltip is shared or split, an array `this.points`
contains all points of the hovered x-value.

Common properties from the Point to use in the formatter include:

- **Point.percentage**:
  Stacked series and pies only. The point's percentage of the total.

- **Point.points**:
  In a shared or split tooltip, this is an array containing all the
  hovered points.

- **this.series**:
  The series object. The series name is available through
  `this.series.name`.

- **this.total**:
  The total value at this point's x value in a stacked series, or the
  sum of all slices in a pie series.

- **this.x**:
  The x value.

- **this.y**:
  The y value.

name: tooltip-header
title: header
description:
Options for the tooltip header when [tooltip.split](#tooltip.split)
is enabled. The header is the box containing the X value in a split
tooltip.

name: tooltip-header-backgroundColor
title: backgroundColor
description:
Background color for the tooltip header when
[tooltip.split](#tooltip.split) is enabled.

name: tooltip-header-borderColor
title: borderColor
description:
Border color for the tooltip header when
[tooltip.split](#tooltip.split) is enabled.

name: tooltip-header-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description:
The width of the border for the tooltip header when
[tooltip.split](#tooltip.split) is enabled.

name: tooltip-header-distance
title: distance
description:
Distance between the plot area and the header (except the
chevron) in a split tooltip, in pixels. The default value makes
the header text align with the axis labels.

name: tooltip-header-shape
title: shape
description:
The name of a symbol to use for the border around the tooltip
header. Applies only when [tooltip.split](#tooltip.split) is
enabled.

Custom callbacks for symbol path generation can also be added to
`Highcharts.SVGRenderer.prototype.symbols` the same way as for
[series.marker.symbol](plotOptions.line.marker.symbol).

name: tooltip-header-style
title: style
description:
CSS styles for the tooltip header. The default is `{ fontSize:
'1em' }`, ensuring that the header text is the same size as the
axis labels.

name: tooltip-headerFormat
title: headerFormat
description:
The HTML of the tooltip header line. The context is the
[Point class](https://api.highcharts.com/class-reference/Highcharts.Point).
Variables are enclosed in curly brackets. Examples of common
variables to include are `x`, `y`, `series.name` and `series.color`
and other properties on the same form. The `point.key` variable
contains the category name, x value or datetime string depending on
the type of axis. For datetime axes, the `point.key` date format can
be set using `tooltip.xDateFormat`.
In v12+, locale-aware date names follow the browser's casing and can
be lower-case, so use the `ucfirst` helper (for example
`{ucfirst point.key}`) if you want a capitalized header.

name: tooltip-hideDelay
title: hideDelay
description:
The number of milliseconds to wait until the tooltip is hidden when
mouse out from a point or chart.

name: tooltip-nullFormat
title: nullFormat
description:
The HTML of the null point's line in the tooltip. Works analogously
to [pointFormat](#tooltip.pointFormat).

name: tooltip-nullFormatter
title: nullFormatter
description:
Callback function to format the text of the tooltip for
visible null points.
Works analogously to [formatter](#tooltip.formatter), including the
`ctx` callback argument added in v12.5.0.

name: tooltip-outside
title: outside
description:
Whether to allow the tooltip to render outside the chart's SVG
element box. By default (`false`), the tooltip is rendered within the
chart's SVG element, which results in the tooltip being aligned
inside the chart area. For small charts, this may result in clipping
or overlapping. When `true`, a separate SVG element is created and
overlaid on the page, allowing the tooltip to be aligned inside the
page itself. Beware that with this option active, CSS classes on the
chart's target container, with classnames matching the pattern
'highcharts-*', will be set on the tooltip as well. This is done to
support theming for tooltips with this option.

Defaults to `true` if `chart.scrollablePlotArea` is activated,
otherwise `false`.

name: tooltip-padding
title: padding
description: Padding inside the tooltip, in pixels.

name: tooltip-pointFormat
title: pointFormat
description:
The HTML of the point's line in the tooltip. The context is the
[Point class](https://api.highcharts.com/class-reference/Highcharts.Point).
Variables are enclosed in curly brackets. Examples of common
variables to include are `x`, `y`, `series.name` and `series.color`
and other properties on the same form. Furthermore, `y` can be
extended by the `tooltip.valuePrefix` and `tooltip.valueSuffix`
variables. This can also be overridden for each series, which makes
it a good hook for displaying units.

In styled mode, the dot is colored by a class name rather than the
point color.

name: tooltip-pointFormatter
title: pointFormatter
description:
A callback function for formatting the HTML output for a single point
in the tooltip. Like the `pointFormat` string, but with more
flexibility. Since v12.6.0, the callback also receives `ctx` as the
first argument, so that arrow functions can access the same context
as regular functions using `this`.

name: tooltip-position
title: position
description:
Positioning options for fixed tooltip, taking effect only when
[tooltip.fixed](#tooltip.fixed) is `true`.

name: tooltip-position-align
title: align
description: The horizontal alignment of the fixed tooltip.

name: tooltip-position-relativeTo
title: relativeTo
description:
